product_title: Spy Tec Z12 Motion Activated Intelligent Security Camcorder Surveillance Camera
review_body:
If the words, "Cheap Chinese Junk" come to your mind when you see this, then congratulate yourself. You're pretty close. One of the most important features of a 'security camera" is the ability to detect motion and record, especially when running on battery and limited storage space. I tested the motion detect on this camera in a few different environments so far (i.e. low light, indoors, outdoors, etc..) and all I got was a SD card full of video triggers. All the testing was done with the low motion sensitivity setting. I can't even imagine what the high one would be.
As others said, the low light operation is poor. I did one of my tests outdoors as the sun was setting. It was good until a point - then the camera started having seizures..it got fuzzy, went to black and white...back to color...then ultimately stabilized with lines across the screen.
Another oddity I noticed was that the firmware reported in the windows config tool seemed later than the latest version posed on the Zetta site. I'm not exactly sure why that is.

It gets two stars because there was one time, in a very light controlled indoor environment, where it didn't constantly trigger, so it MAY have some usefulness for your particular situation. In adequate light, the video isn't too bad (you don't need HD for most security applications).

The are a variety of settings that are configurable, which is quite nice. One setting that could, and should, be configurable is the amount of time it will record after the last trigger is detected. The manual states that this is 5 minutes. So, if someone enters the picture for 30 seconds then leaves, you conceivably would have 5 minutes of recording nothing afterwards. This isn't power or memory efficient.

My original thought was to return this, but I want to crack it open and look at some of the internals. I may decide to make my own.

I will continue to test and report any new developments.

product_title: Polaroid ZIP Mobile Printer Parent ASIN
review_body:
The printer came in a small fairly plain box with decent packaging. Upon opening the packaging it comes with a pack of paper, and a pain charging cable. On the plus side it comes fully charged and ready to print

I went to load the paper into the printer, and there are warnings about not to bend the paper, leave it in the car, standard stuff. Loading the printer was as easy as sliding the top off, and dropping the pack barcode down in the printer. Getting the top back on required a few flips to find the right direction since it doesn't clearly line up which side the top slides back on from.

Note that the 2x3 print size is actually very small. This should be obvious by the sizing, but make sure you understand what you are buying. These aren't normal 3x5 photos even.

My first attempt to print was using a non rooted android one plus one running lollipop(oxygen OS). I went to the app store and downloaded the Zink app. For some reason the app caused my phone to work very hard and heat up, I haven't had issues with other apps doing this. One thing I did notice while using the app was NFC options. Which is neat you just put your phone on the printer and it loads up the app for you, very convenient and a nice touch.

While using the app it crashed several times on initial launch. I tried to bluetooth pair the printer outside of the app and after a few attempts I was able to get it to pair. However I was unable to print from the app with pairing the printer from the standard android bluetooth menu. I deleted the pairing and initiated the pair from within the app, this time it worked.

When I finally got the printer working it popped up telling me there was a critical firmware update for the printer. I let it download and apply the update via bluetooth. It took about 5 minutes to update, and the instructions said to wait for the printer to restart. The printer never restarted and required a power on, but the update worked successfully.

I did find quite a few issues with the app. The estimated percentage complete for sending to printer / printing was wildly inaccurate. I received several out of memory errors when trying to load larger pictures.

I also tried the same setup from an iPhone 6. I downloaded the app, but was not given an option to pair bluetooth from within the app. I did it from the system menu and it worked fine. I didn't experience any crashes with smaller pictures. The percentage completion bar was also more accurate.

Printing take approximately 40 seconds to send to printer, and another 35 seconds to print. While the printer is printing, it is pretty quiet. It does have a bit of a high pitch tone to it, which could get annoying to some people. The first print takes a bit longer since it "prints" the barcode you use when loading the printer.

As for the quality of the prints, I used very high resolution DSLR pictures to try to pull the best photos possible from the little printer. I noticed the colors are slightly muted, and the picture overall a bit darker. Contrast was fairly low and there was a brownish tint to the photos, which almost looked like the standard instagram filter. There was discoloring around the edges, and darker parts of photos were crushed into black. Some of the patterns such as on shirts, or with strands of hair remained, but gradual transitions looked muddy and unable to differentiate.

The resolution was OK for the size of the photo. They look fine from 1-2ft away. Some of the photos I printed I aimed to capitalize on the look of the prints, including a nearly black and white photo of a flower. These turned out really well. While printing photos straight from the iPhone / One Plus One's camera resulted in even more muddying and lack of definition.

I was not able to smudge the images after printing, and the printer didn't seem to get too hot. Based on battery life I would estimate around 10-15 prints max per charge. There is an auto power off setting, but it seems the actual printing takes the majority of the battery.

The prints end up being very expensive with the proprietary paper you have to buy. Instead of making money on ink/film/the device, they are clearly aiming to make the profit on the paper. Also note that I was provided a sample of this product for my unbiased review.

----------------------------------------------
Pros:
* Cool concept
* Makes stickers
* Decent battery life
* Fairly quick printing

Cons:
* The quality of prints are low
* Android app needs work
* Very expensive per print
* Very small print size.

In conclusion I would say this printer would be neat to print a quick sticker to put on something. Or for younger kids to enjoy the printed results. These are obviously not archival quality, or even enough quality to give to family members. product_title: Deecam D200 1280x720P HD H.264 Wireless/Wired IP Camera with Two-Way Audio IR-Cut Filter Nithgt Vision Pan/Tilt Control, QR Code Scan Phone remote monitoring supported (Black)
review_body:
The Tenvis D200 (aka Tenvis TH661, Deecam D200) is a network-attached camera. The box contains the following:
• The camera
• Ethernet (network) cable
• Power adapter
• Mounting bracket, with screws and wall plugs
• Software CD (Mini CD)
• Manual

The camera housing is made of shiny black plastic but it feels nicely weighted and solid. There's a wifi antenna on the back (it doesn't appear to be replaceable, unfortunately), a Micro SD/SDHC card slot (documentation claims that cards up to 32GB are supported - I had no problems using a 32GB card), an Ethernet port and a socket for the power adapter. The manual is surprisingly good - it covers the initial setup steps clearly. The manual and provided software is also available online (see below).

Setup is straightforward. I connected it to my wired network and it found an IP address within a few seconds. I did initial setup using the Life Online app on my iPhone but it's also possible to use the Tenvis app (available for Apple iOS and Android). The camera supports both wired and wireless connections - the wireless worked fine for me (2.4GHz only) but I prefer using the wired connection for performance/stability reasons. Connectivity to your wireless network can be setup using the app.

In addition to managing the camera using a mobile app, there is also a web interface - just browse to the IP address that the camera is on and log in with your administrator username and password. The web interface allows you to configure far more options than the mobile app. For example, it allows for some advanced functions like triggering an ftp upload of a photo/video or email from an alert, which is very useful. If you're unsure of the address of your camera, you can use the provided Tenvis Search Tool, which will find it automatically (this works for Windows and Mac). You can also view the camera feed from the web interface and I had no problem accessing it from a Mac.

In use, I'm very impressed with this camera. The image quality is excellent, both during the day and at night, and maximum resolution is 1280x720 (ie 720p). Setting up alerts (to record when movement is detected) is very easy and works well but you will need to provide an SD/SDHC card to record to the camera itself. Another thing I like is that it's easy to move the camera (tilt and pan) remotely. Unfortunately movement below the horizontal is limited, so if you're not using the bracket, don't mount it too high up otherwise you won't be able to see too far below the camera's position. But that's a minor criticism, really.

The camera has a built-in microphone and can record audio. I can also be used for two way communication but I found it a bit clunky as you need to switch modes in the app from listening to speaking each time you want to say something and then hear the response.

Note: Disable the UPnP and P2P settings on the camera or make sure the appropriate ports are blocked on your router so that your camera is not accessible from the Internet. In the past some models of Tenvis cameras have had security problems (just search online for "Tenvis security hole") so you *do not* want these cameras exposed to the Internet.

Pros:
+ Easy to set up
+ Very good image quality, both during the day and at night
+ Excellent functionality
+ Fully-featured web interface

Cons:
- Limited movement below the horizontal
- Two-way audio a bit clunky
- Very important: make sure you disable the UPnP/P2P functionality

As mentioned, you can download the manuals and additional software online (just search for "Tenvis D200" or "Tenvis TH661" for this particular model).

Overall, I'm very impressed with this camera. It offers a lot of features for the money - for under $60, it's a bargain. Highly recommended. Note - this camera may be available froma few sellers, so make sure you price compare before buying!s, so make sure you price compare before buying!

review_body:
The microscope came packaged very well, which was a relief compared to some prior experiences I have had. Packed inside the box is the USB microscope, stand, USB cable, an installation software (CD) a manual, a quick start guide, and calibration chart. However, if you do not have a CD< you can get the manual and software online. Assembly was easy and intuitive, taking about one minute. The software installed on my Dell Windows 7 system with no issues.

Simply plug the microscope into the computer and you are off and running. The software of course interfaces with the computer and does so exceedingly well. You can even open the interface software to a full window. To view objects, one knob provides general control and the other provides fine tuning. This is perhaps where a more expensive unit might be better suited for some. The fine tuning takes effort. A variable light adjustment is provided on the cable, as well as a trigger/shutter control for the camera. The shutter button works very well and the software provides a means of organizing your images. It is important to remember that there is no viewing piece on the microscope. Instead, you view images on your computer. Magnification, up to 330x, is controlled through the software.

The general design of the microscope is good for the intended purpose. The base is heavy enough and seems secure. Enough control points are provided, allowing you to hold down slides. Note- I was provided a sample for a no obligation review.

review_body: We have had the Kodak CFH-V15 for a week now.  The camera itself is good, but I think the app is buggy.  It tends to just sit there and churn when I click on my camera to view it. There is a 2-3 sec delay on the video, which is okay, but sometimes the app freezes, so it doesn't show the correct picture.  However, you can turn the mic on and listen to what is happening?  But what good is that.  You have to manually turn of event recording while you are home, or else you get videos of you and your family doing your normal routines.  The free 1-day cloud storage is good, and most products don't have that.  Quality of the picture is very good whether day or night.  However, if you leave it on auto, it will probably be on night vision (black/white) when not home, as not enough lighting. I have to set it to off during the day, so I can see in color.  Alerts are very good, and spot on.  But I would only use that when away from your house, or else you will get a lot of phone alerts, unless you turn off event recording or the mobile alerts.  I would give it 5 stars if it weren't for the phone app.  You can pan/tilt, but it's not a continuous movement, almost in frames, if that makes sense.  You can also manually set to record, but haven't checked to see how long it will run.  Overall good product, just wish they would fix the app issues, because those get frustrating.  Considering sending back and getting something else, but can't seem to find something better in the same price range with free cloud storage.  So really, really hoping they fix the app issues :)

product_title: Kodak CFH-V15 - HD WiFi Video Monitoring Surveillance Security Camera, Pan/Tilt, Two-Way Audio, Night Vision & Free Cloud Storage
review_body:
I have been using the Kodak CFH-V15 for the past month and I must say that I've been impressed. I will note right away, if you do not own an iPhone are android phone this camera will likely not work for you. The setup is done through the app and without a phone that supports the app you will not be able to set the camera up.

I found the camera setup to be relativity easy. You plug the camera in and then open up the app on your phone. From there you connect to the camera and setup the wifi password so that it can connect to your home network. One downside I did notice is that there is not a native app for the iPad. Because of this I ended up downloading the iPhone version of the app to my iPad and set it up that way. It would be nice if Kodak would make the app universal so that it wasn't so ugly on the iPad. This was my only complaint with the setup process.

Using the camera for daily use is a breeze. The video quality is excellent and the pan/tilt feature allows you to see an entire room easily. The app also works well and allows you to set up notifications to alert you if motion is detected. This ensures that you will not miss anything moving in the room that you have the camera setup in. The app also gives you the ability to speak through a speaker that is on the camera, so if you have a pet you could easily speak to them remotely.

Overall I would say that this camera is an excellent option for anyone that is looking for a home security camera. The quality is excellent and while the app is not the greatest, it does do its job well enough.

product_title: Korner Extender
review_body:
I've been looking for a system like Korner for a number of years without success. Living in crime-ridden South Africa and having been the victim of armed house robbery myself, I just had to get a back-up system for my existing system (passive infrared radio- alarm linked to response company) to give additional peace of mind. Eventually I resorted to a Chinese GSM system but if you have ever tried that out you will know the term ' user unfriendly' was specifically created to decribe those systems. In came Korner and what a pleasant experience!
A few remarks:
One piece door contacts and real pleasing on the eye!
Absolutely user friendly - even a child can install them.
Direct control via an App on your phone.
Long battery life
The whole system is plug and play.
Korner will send you an email as well as a pop-up on your phone if intrusion is detected.
Korner can be used as a door chime if not armed - so you can still monitor movement through the house even when it is disarmed.
Allthough the tags are meant to be used with doors/windows, I've dropped one in portable safebox at home and it works perfectly well to register movement of the box.
Very nice feature is that you can actually set up a circle of friends to be notified of intrusions - one can create your own personal neighbourhood watch system.
Customer service is excellent - I had a few questions/issues and time and again I was assisted in a prompt and efficient manner. Love the fact that the system is updated continiously (OTA) with new features and improvements.
The whole system is portable - so you can take it along if you move.
It deserves a 5/5.
Francois, South Africa

review_body:
Unfortunately, it's just another faulty action cam. Too bad, I really, really wanted this device to be the answer to an otherwise expensive prayer. I got this for my husband who has been looking at the GoPro devices. I didn't want him spending $300-400 on a 'toy' so I picked this one out for him. It seems like a great idea: inexpensive action camera with GoPro mounting compatibility and lots of accessories as well.

We got it and he put it on his motorcycle to get some video of his daily commute and travels. It appears to have worked well for about 25 miles, then the video went wacky; in and out of focus, strange colors (it was shot at night, since that's when he goes to work), so something happened while it was mounted on the bike. The next morning he shot his ride home during daylight and it became evident what happened: the IR pass filter had come loose and was wiggling about in the housing, causing color and focus issues.

Too bad. We did find the 'entry' level [[ASIN:B00NIYNUXO GoPro HERO (No Wi-Fi)]]and we'll give that a try next, but this one had to go back! :( Other than that, this really seemed like a great little unit with features that GoPro has for $300. Great quality case and the wifi funtionality worked great. The colors and pictures seemed high quality (until it went south, of course) If one or the other of these Asian companies would institute a higher level of quality control, they could really rule the action cam market. Oh well, two stars for the effort though!

review_body:
I wanted to fall in love with it but it had too many issues. I've used the 560 III and IV and loved them! Some issues I had with this unit were related to Master/Slave wireless sync but it was a Canon related problem (camera related -- I have a 5D Mark2 which I still use as a backup). Heads up if you're using this on a Canon 5DMark2! On the newer 5DMark3 the issues are resolved.

What I could not get past was battery power usage. I have never had a flash unit that would eat up through batteries so fast! Some users complained about the unit wasting battery power when off. I did not test that so I can't say for sure. But under normal use, the same use as my old 560III's or the newer 560IV's, these things were abysmal! During a wedding, I'd be busy changing batteries all night long! Never an issue with the aforementioned units, which I'm still successfully using.

Also, the firmware upgrade can ONLY be done on a Windows 32bit operating system. Insane! I don't even have access to a "32bit" Windows OS anymore!

Otherwise, the design, menus, etc are great. Everything else worked and quite well. I shoot in Manual all the time so TTL is pretty useless to me but it worked well when tested. HSS also worked well. It's a new product. I'm sure subsequent versions will have these issues fixed. When they fix them, this flash will be a great thing to have!

Sent them back. Really felt bad about it because I was really happy to have them but they just didn't work for me (yet).

product_title: Canon ELPH 340
review_body:
At first glance the 340HS seems to be a technical triumph, squeezing 12x zoom into a camera that is almost exactly the same size as it's predecessor, the 330HS, which had 10X zoom. It has rounded corners and a big screen, making the camera look good. But I have concluded that In spite of increasing the optical zoom range, and increasing the imager from 12 to 16 megapixels, the 340HS is not as good a camera as it's predecessor, the 330HS. I own both.

The 330HS has the Digic5 processor, which is faster and allows the use of 3200 and 6400 ISO speeds with some loss of color quality but not horrible colored snow. The 340HS has the older Digic4 processor which is capped at ISO 3200, and cannot take full images at the burst speed that the 330HS will do. While increasing the optical zoom the designers reduced the maximum aperture from f3.0 to f3.6. In low light you have the triple disadvantages of a slower lens, a less-capable processor, and more pixels crowded on an imager of the same size.

But the worst part is that many of the manual features available on the 330HS are not present on the 340HS. One that I miss is forced flash, such as you might want to use when your subject is backlighted by a window. The camera also displays a ridiculous set of altered photos, including monochrome, of every photo you take.

My 330HS connects wirelessly to my computer but I've been unable to get the 340HS to do so in spite of reading the manual and using Canon's wifi connection software. I've read that others have made the connection successfully.

The 340HS appears to be a triumph of style over substance. Canon can do better.

product_title: Vimtag, IP/Network ,Wireless, Video Monitoring, Surveillance, security camera
review_body: UPDATE: At one point along the way some firmware updates or such has made me downgrade my rating from 2-star to 1-star. While the footage does record, I am unable to access the card from PC including after unmounting from the camera setting. I am always asked to format it on my PC. I've tried three different computers and four memory sticks. It seems now the only way to get footage off is by clicking 'download' through the web interface and waiting in real-time for the footage to transfer. The interface is still just as horrendous and unusable as it was when I wrote my initial review so long ago.  The camera quality is acceptable but nothing out of the ordinary these days (it is comparable to the 808 #16 keychain camera, if that). It was easy enough to connect (you have to use physical LAN cable at first) but the built-in WiFi is weak and I found difficulty getting steady signal when it was placed one floor below while the rest of my WiFi-enabled devices worked fine. My biggest gripe is the horrendous interface they force upon you when accessing the camera through the web interface. First you are prompted to install some very cryptic and unknown proprietary plugin / ActiveX control that links to the "Shenzhm Mining Technology" website, which I guess is an affiliation of the developer of this camera. To get motion recording to work you have to enable the alarm action as well (which bombards your phone with notifactions with each motion until you disable notifications via the phone settings), and you cannot use the scheduler if using motion detection. I have set this up to point outside but had to then buy a mechanical timer to power the camera off at night and on in the day since there is no way to remotely power it off or schedule motion recording for only a particular period of time. When you want to see what has been recorded through the Web interface, you go to the "Messages" screen where each record appears twice (once for 'alarm motion' and oncefor 'record'). Only 30 rows are shown at a time and the thumbnail snapshots are microscopic at 80x40 pixels. You can view a larger snapshot by clicking the thumbnail but can only view one snapshot at a time and have to close it to open another instead of just having a prev/next button. The videos have no controls for playback and there is no natural way to download them from the device without taking the MicroSD card out. When you want to see more records you have to endlessly click "More30Records" which is a terrible UX design. I have taken to the extreme of manually modifying styles and local script behavior via Stylish and GreaseMonkey plugins to make the interface slightly more bearable. If you know the device's IP you can connect locally, connecting through their own site for viewing was very sluggish. Next time around I would spend a little more money for a more industry-standard IP camera.

product_title: Samsung WB35F 16.2MP Smart WiFi & NFC Digital Camera with 12x Optical Zoom and 2.7" LCD
review_body: --- UPDATE: This camera was likely just defective. The seller sold it from Singapore without disclosing it, so I didn't have warranty coverage in the U.S., but Amazon refunded me. There weren't any others of the same model available by that point, so I don't know for sure whether my issue was a one-off. But I sure hope so! ---  In replacing a Canon that cost just $70 over two years ago ([[ASIN:B004HW73S4 Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Black)]]), I didn't have very demanding needs: I wanted a better zoom and USB charging instead of AA batteries, and similar or better picture quality. This Samsung made a good first impression but didn't live up to that standard.  It starts by turning on super-quickly, a revelation compared to my old Canon. But looks were deceiving -- you can't actually take a picture for the first few seconds after it comes on. The zoom pops out and the screen lights up, but if you press the button to take the picture, it gives you nothing. You have to release, wait a few seconds, then try again. Utterly infuriating when you've whipped out the camera to try and quickly shoot something before it's gone.  The picture quality also ranges wildly, from decent to unacceptable. A large number of pictures come out unfocused, and no adjustments changed that view from being a complete blur. At other times, colors come out fine at one second and unnatural the next, as in the examples. (White cars on a sunny day were particularly susceptible to being badly washed out.) Most of the time the camera's screen is clear enough to let you know that you have a bad picture and should try again; others no.  The camera isn't without merits. The zoom is great for such a compact camera, the WiFi was a nice feature, and the battery seems to have a pretty long life. But I can't count on it to take an adequate picture, to the point that on a recent trip I ended up ditching it into my backpack and settling for my phone. I'd figured that reliably taking okay pictures was a given even at a fairly low price, but apparently that's no longer the case. I'll be buying something higher-end.

product_title: Deecam D200 1280x720P HD H.264 Wireless/Wired IP Camera with Two-Way Audio IR-Cut Filter Night Vision Pan/Tilt Control, QR Code Scan Phone remote monitoring supported (Black)
review_body:
The Deecam D200 (aka Tenvis TH661, Tenvis D200) is a network-attached camera. The box contains the following:
• The camera
• Ethernet (network) cable
• Power adapter
• Mounting bracket, with screws and wall plugs
• Software CD (Mini CD)
• Manual

The camera housing is made of shiny black plastic but it feels nicely weighted and solid. There's a wifi antenna on the back (it doesn't appear to be replaceable, unfortunately), a Micro SD/SDHC card slot (documentation claims that cards up to 32GB are supported - I had no problems using a 32GB card), an Ethernet port and a socket for the power adapter. The manual is surprisingly good - it covers the initial setup steps clearly. The manual and provided software is also available online (see below).

Setup is straightforward. I connected it to my wired network and it found an IP address within a few seconds. I did initial setup using the Life Online app on my iPhone but it's also possible to use the Tenvis app (available for Apple iOS and Android). The camera supports both wired and wireless connections - the wireless worked fine for me (2.4GHz only) but I prefer using the wired connection for performance/stability reasons. Connectivity to your wireless network can be setup using the app.

In addition to managing the camera using a mobile app, there is also a web interface - just browse to the IP address that the camera is on and log in with your administrator username and password. The web interface allows you to configure far more options than the mobile app. For example, it allows for some advanced functions like triggering an ftp upload of a photo/video or email from an alert, which is very useful. If you're unsure of the address of your camera, you can use the provided Tenvis Search Tool, which will find it automatically (this works for Windows and Mac). You can also view the camera feed from the web interface and I had no problem accessing it from a Mac.

In use, I'm very impressed with this camera. The image quality is excellent, both during the day and at night, and maximum resolution is 1280x720 (ie 720p). Setting up alerts (to record when movement is detected) is very easy and works well but you will need to provide an SD/SDHC card to record to the camera itself. Another thing I like is that it's easy to move the camera (tilt and pan) remotely. Unfortunately movement below the horizontal is limited, so if you're not using the bracket, don't mount it too high up otherwise you won't be able to see too far below the camera's position. But that's a minor criticism, really.

The camera has a built-in microphone and can record audio. I can also be used for two way communication but I found it a bit clunky as you need to switch modes in the app from listening to speaking each time you want to say something and then hear the response.

Note: Disable the UPnP and P2P settings on the camera or make sure the appropriate ports are blocked on your router so that your camera is not accessible from the Internet. In the past some models of Tenvis cameras have had security problems (just search online for "Tenvis security hole") so you *do not* want these cameras exposed to the Internet.

Pros:
+ Easy to set up
+ Very good image quality, both during the day and at night
+ Excellent functionality
+ Fully-featured web interface

Cons:
- Limited movement below the horizontal
- Two-way audio a bit clunky
- Very important: make sure you disable the UPnP/P2P functionality

As mentioned, you can download the manuals and additional software online (just search for "Tenvis D200" or "Tenvis TH661" for this particular model).

Overall, I'm very impressed with this camera. It offers a lot of features for the money - for under $60, it's a bargain. Highly recommended. Note - this camera may be available froma few sellers, so make sure you price compare before buying!s, so make sure you price compare before buying!

review_body: This is the first lens I bought for my Lumix G1, the reason, having no experience with Lumix lenses, was that Panasonic claimed that this lens was developed by Leica for the M4/3 system.  I have owned this lens for many years now. Frankly, I have not been disappointed.  The lens is impressive as it yields sharp balanced images,  I was not really expecting much at the the time, but it has proven to be a good value.  Since then I have bought many other Lumix and Leica lenses for my G1 and GX7, but I still use this lens frequently.  Last week I decided to give away my entire Nikon system that I used in my profession, a tough decision letting go of and old friend, but I had not really picked it up since I bought this lens. This lens has dampened focusing, or so it seems, and is easy to focus accurately, it is certainly a faster focusing lens than my equivalent Nikkors.  It is light weight.  I carry it in a fishing vest, along with several other lenses. and it gets bounce and banged around when I scurry up and down slopes to get a good position and it has held up well.  In terms of image characteristics it performs similar to my Zeiss lenses on my Hasselblad.  I like to make oversized prints and this lens serves well.  Lumix makes so many good lenses it is hard to know which to buy, I don't regret this purchase.  As a user of may old lenses by Zeiss, Leica and Schneider I would put this lens in the same class. The selection of glass has always been highly subjective relative to one's photographic tastes, so look at some test images to get a feel for the lens.  I really like it.

[[VIDEOID:902e8616169ea6ef371d58868ce0a0e]] ✏️ Quick thoughts to supplement my video demonstration.

Everything you need is included except for a monitor (one that accepts either HDMI or VGA) and a hard drive (just a basic laptop hard drive, \\"SATA\\" like this one: [[ASIN:B00AAKF8KC Generic 320 GB 320GB 2.5 Inch Sata Laptop Internal Hard drive 5400 RPM For Laptop/Mac/PS3 (320 GB)]].

I like this security system because:
- It's very easy to setup. Yes it takes a while (lots of steps) but it's relatively easy compared to other systems.
- There are a ton of features--everything from motion detection (which works wonderful) to an email alert system when it detects something (you have to be hooked up to a wired network of course). You can also schedule out when exactly you want it to record (e.g. after business hours).

- Very smooth, excellent quality footage. Not like that choppy stuff you see on old CCTV security systems.
- Tons of long cables. 60 foot cables (8 of them!). Note: Due to the length of the cable, there's a slight 1 second delay from the event to when you see it on your monitor.
- Full metal, tough camera design.
- Awesome in low-light/darkness. Infrared lights work wonderfully to light up the room when it's dark. (of course the human eye can't see infrared, but it lights up enough for the camera to film everything)
- Incredibly good price here on Amazon. Just factor in a hard drive and a monitor.

Overall I am very impressed with this camera system. An excellent bang for your buck, especially considering how many cameras they give you.

product_title: GE Security TX-6010-01-1 Supervised Wireless Smoke, Residential UL217 Transmitter
review_body: Luckily I haven't had a real-life situation where this unit was needed, but setup and pairing with my Concord 4 system took about 3 minutes. If you are using a GE or Interlogix panel with this model it should be very easy to add to your existing system. Be sure to download your wireless panel's user manual, as you these smoke alarms usually need to go onto a dedicated group/zone, and be setup as a specific sensor. If you are using a monitored Concord 4 system, be sure to add the sensor text as "smoke or fire alarm," and perhaps a location (which I did not as I don't really care where the fire or smoke is, I just want to know my house is on fire) so that the monitoring company will know that it's a fire emergency and not a police emergency. If you don't name this sensor I believe it will only tell the monitoring company that Sensor #XX has been tripped. I would recommend getting more than one unit for your home, and installing these yourself as it's free. It's definitely simple enough to do by yourself, provided you follow the instructions closely.  Update: My spouse burned some bacon this morning and this thing definitely works. It's quite sensitive. It's not in the kitchen but near it.

product_title: BAXIA TECHNOLOGY Accessories Kit for GoPro HERO 4 Black Silver GoPro HERO 3+ Black Silver GoPro HERO 3 Black Silver GoPro HERO 2 Black Silver Accessories for GoPro 4 3+ 3 2 1 Camera Accessory Bundle Kit for SJ4000 SJ5000 SJ6000 in Skiing Parachuting Swimming Rowing Surfing Climbing Running Bike Riding Camping Diving Outing and Any Other Outdoor Sports
review_body:
If you own a GoPro Camera, chances are you have realized that there are literally thousands of accessories on the market for it. Some accessory kits include one or two items, and you have to buy dozens of different kits in order to get everything that you need. This kit from Baxia Technology literally has everything that you need for your GoPro Camera.

First of all, I was overwhelmed by the number of pieces included in this set. I know it states exactly what is included, but wow, when you see it all together, it's a lot of pieces. You immediately wonder will I ever use all of this? And chances are, you won't. But, if you have a GoPro Camera, you will probably use a good portion of it. I waited awhile to write this review because I wanted a chance to truly test each part of this kit before writing the review.

The very first thing I noticed about this kit was that there are no instructions. None whatsoever. There is nothing labeling the pieces that are included, no booklet showing you how to use the included pieces, and no usage tips or tricks. Basically you are left to figure things out, and if you can't, you are up a creek because there is no documentation, not even a product box to help you. All of these pieces come in a resealable bag, similar to a Ziploc, not very sturdy for the number of pieces included. There is a very nice velvet pouch with a drawstring included that is black and says Baxia on it. I don't know about you, but I hate to be a walking advertisement for companies, so I was disappointed to see their logo on the pouch, especially since it will be holding GoPro Camera accessories, which no one will know or recognize the Baxia name in association with it.

Here is what is included:
Head belt strap mount
Chest belt strap mount
Helmet strap mount
Extendable handle monopod
Floating handle grip
Floating block with 3M adhesive pad
Wrist strap mount
360 degree rotary clip mount
Bike handlebar holder mount
Adjustable car suction cup mount
Three way adjustable pivot arm with surface quick release buckle
Three way adjustable pivot arm without surface quick release buckle
2 tripod mount adapters
2 surface J hook buckles
2 surface quick release buckles
3 long screw bolts
1 short screw bolt
2 flat mounts
2 arc mounts
5 flat 3M adhesive pads
5 curved mount adhesive pads
Storage pouch
Safety buckle

The strap mounts are really well made, but they are definitely not one size fits all. I would say they are more like one size fits most. The head belt strap is very comfortable and does not dig in to you as long as you have a relatively normal sized head. If you have a head that's on the larger side, you will find it uncomfortable. The chest belt strap mount is great if you are a size XL or smaller, again, very comfortable, but if you are on the larger side, you'll find the strap uncomfortable. The helmet strap really depends on the helmet. It fit on two bike helmets we tried, but didn't fit a third. It fit on two skateboard helmets, but wouldn't fit a roller blade helmet, and unfortunately it doesn't fit motorcycle helmets. The wrist strap mount will comfortably fit a 7 or 8 inch wrist, but it did not fit comfortably on a plus sized wrist (9" wrist).

The straps overall are very comfortable, do not dig into you, and enable you to mount the GoPro Camera securely, so it doesn't feel like it's going to fall.

The monopod is one of the best pieces in this kit. Very high quality and extends out like crazy (almost 40"). It holds the GoPro Camera very tightly and securely, and it doesn't feel like the camera is too top heavy even when it's fully extended. It makes it great for capturing scenes that are far away, or when there is a large crowd of people. I have seen monopods alone sell for a little over half the price of this kit, and it's most definitely high quality, and not a cheap plastic monopod like some I have seen.

The floating pieces in this kit are the "weak link" in my opinion. The floating handle grip does in fact float, but it's not heavy enough to keep your camera from going for a swim, and getting away from you. The floating block is very disappointing as well, because as soon as it gets fully saturated, it no longer floats on top of the water, but sort of tries to bob just under the surface of the water. The floating handle grip looks so nice, it just is no match for the heavy GoPro Camera.

The 360 degree rotary clip mount is awesome, and I mean awesome. The clip on this mount is the most amazing clip that I have ever seen on a camera accessory. It will clip to literally anything and is very durable. The teeth tightly clamp down on the surface that you clipped it to, and it does not cause any kind of damage to the clip. The clip is pretty much unbreakable, I tried clipping it to a variety of different surfaces...plastic, metal, steel, chrome, and it clipped tightly to each surface without any problems or slipping.

The bike handlebar holder mount is pretty weak. It fits some bikes that don't have thicker bars, but didn't fit either the mountain bike or road bike that we tried it on. It fit well on the beach cruiser bike though. I was disappointed with the fit of it, and even when there was a good fit, like on the beach cruiser, the mount would slide around and not stay firmly in place. It is one of the weaker mounts in the kit in my opinion.

The adjustable car suction cup mount is another awesome product in this kit, for me, the price of this item and the price of the monopod alone make this kit worthwhile. The suction cup is the kind that is tight fitting and it doesn't slide around. It stays firmly on not only car dash boards, but also on the windshield, and on non car surfaces like filing cabinets and counter tops. This is one of my favorite mounts included in this set. It literally attaches to everything. It holds the GoPro Camera so tightly you don't have to worry about things getting out of control while you are using it.

The pivot arms are so so. One has a quick release buckle and one doesn't. The quick release buckle to me makes the pivot arm feel "less secure" because I worry about it releasing on it's own. It hasn't yet, but it feels like it could. The pivot arms don't really hold the GoPro Camera tightly. They felt weak compared to the other mounts in this set. The tripod mount adapters are really nice and give extra stability to the GoPro Camera when it's mounted on a tripod. It feels like the GoPro isn't going anywhere, and that's a great feeling.

The buckles are very high quality. They don't become "less tight" with continuous use. The J hook buckles are my favorite they feel like they really provide the GoPro the support it needs and won't weaken over time. They are made of really high quality materials and they don't have the whiting or fading that some buckles do with continued use. The quick release buckles, I'm not a fan of, and I've stopped using them, they just don't feel like they stay securely in place to me, no matter what I tried.

The screw bolts are very well made, and there are 3 long ones and 1 short one. They are very nice, sturdy, and are not cheap feeling at all. They fit a variety of cameras, not just the GoPro which is nice. They are made of plastic with metal bolts, but it's not really weak plastic and feels substantial.

The mounts are extremely well made and durable. They don't bend while in use, or cave in under the weight of the GoPro, something I was worried about when I first saw them. There are two flat mounts and 2 arc mounts, and they are easy to mount and then un-mount using the included 3M adhesives.

While I'm talking about the 3M adhesives, most of them were unusable. Because all of the pieces in this kit are just tossed into a bag, the 3M adhesives were bent in the shipping process, and when removed from the bag, some of them no longer had the protective coverings on, some were too bent to use, and some didn't stick at all. Out of the 5 flat adhesive pads, one was sticky enough to use. Out of the 5 curved mount adhesive pads 2 were sticky enough to use. I tried some of those that were bent and no longer felt sticky, but there was no getting them to stick. Getting the 3M adhesive off of the surface once stuck also proved to be challenging and I was happy to have Goo Gone standing by which worked wonders. I would like to see them be no mess adhesives that didn't leave goo behind on your surfaces.

At the end of the day, there are some really useful pieces in this kit (the clip, the monopod, and the car mount to name three); there are some pieces that I wish worked better (like the floating pieces); and there are some things that missed the mark all together (the 3M adhesives, the lack of instructions to name two). It's a good kit, but not a great kit. Is it a must have for a GoPro Camera, not really. There are some pieces you will use and a lot of "fluff" pieces that you likely won't use, depending on how you use your GoPro Camera.

product_title: Nikon Coolpix L15 8MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Vibration Reduction Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL)
review_body:
I got this camera as a gift way back in 2007. Obviously, camera technology has improved a lot over the past couple years, and this camera hasn't really withstood the test of time. I didn't really need a point and shoot camera back in 2007 so I just kind of stuffed this thing in my closet and forgot about it. Now, I realized I wanted a cheap point and shoot for taking short videos during my upcoming cruise. So I busted this out of my closet to see if it still worked. Luckily, it did. I've been playing with it for the past few days, and here's what I've observed:

Pros:
-Picture Quality: Shoots decent quality photos/video (I wasn't expecting much, but the picture quality is pretty good. It's about on par with my iPhone 5.)
-Easy to Use: Simple and easy to use (It's bare bones, but all the controls and menus are pretty intuitive.)
-Feels Good: The camera feels good in my hand. It's easy to hold and has a good weight to it.
-Tripod Mount: Has a place for a tripod

Cons:
-Battery Life: It takes 2 AA batteries, which may be a con for some people and may be a pro for others. However, the batteries don't last very long. I put in 2 brand new batteries and they died after shooting about 15 minutes of video and taking 3 pictures. I thought maybe I had used some bad batteries, so I tried again with 2 new ones. Same thing, died after about 15 minutes of video. Not sure how many pictures you can take with the battery life though.
-Memory Card Placement: The memory card slot is in the same place the batteries are. So every time you need to change/remove the memory card, you have to finagle around the batteries which fall out easily. Not a huge deal, but still a slight annoyance.

Overall, this is a good camera to just goof around with, maybe give it to a young kid. I wouldn't use this as your go-to camera, especially if you want to shoot video.

product_title: Celestron 44126 Micro360+ Microscope with 2MP Imager
review_body: I have a Celestron telescope and binoculars which I am happy with, so when it was time to buy a Microscope for my girlfriend, I thought "Needs to be Celestron".  How wrong could I be?  The quality control is a joke  The first one I ordered came without the Camera and other pieces missing in the box.  When the replacement finally arrives (thanks Amazon), the bottom light kept switching on and off randomly.  I finally unscrewed the cover of the light and the bulb wasn't put in correctly. product_title: Foscam 2 Megapixel Network Camera - Color FI9900P
review_body: Looking for an exterior IP camera, I was impressed by the specs for the new Foscam FI9900P HD 1080p bullet camera, and ordered one to try out and add to my home surveillance setup. I first looked at what reviews I could find, such as the couple of reviews on Youtube and a few on Amazon. Since it is such a new camera there is not a lot of info out there, so I was taking a bit of risk.  First thing upon receipt was to connect up my laptop to the camera directly, and get the IP set up and so on. I found that in the current generation of firmware, you are now forced to change the user name and password immediately, a good thing. However what is not made clear is that the firmware will no longer accept a new “weak” password – the new password must be either “medium” or “strong” to be accepted. The error message from the Foscam Client rejecting your new password attempts doesn’t make this clear. A bit of trial and error, and I figured it out.  Next step was to upgrade the firmware. The instructions on the firmware update downloaded from the Foscam site are pretty detailed and clear. System firmware version: 1.11.1.4, App firmware version: 2.74.1.7_p1, Plug-in version: 3.3.0.7. Now time to check out more fully.  The basics worked via the Foscam Client. While I have not had hardware problems with Foscam cams, I have always had problems trying to use their various applications, and so use their camera for the hardware functionality ONLY, and rely on a Synology NAS box running Surveillance Station 7 to talk to the cameras and do the data storage, motion detection, remote access, all outside of the cameras. Surveillance Station and their iOS application DS Cam are both very solid in my experience. Looking to Foscam software to do this functionality is "problematic" to put it kindly - look at the reams of postings over months and years with problems. Give up and look for another solution, don't expect that a firmware update will miraculously solve this.When I tried to add the new FI9900P to Synology Surveillance Station, no luck. From a quick check online I found that this camera is not yet supported in native form by applications such as Blue Iris or Synology Surveillance Station. That is not a surprise for a new camera, and hopefully will be addressed in the days ahead.  Initially I was unable to connect to the camera from Synology SS even as a Generic Camera, using the standard ONVIF protocol. I tried both Synology SS 7, and the open source utility ONVIF Device Manager v2.2.250. I was able to connect up to my FI19831P cameras on the same network on non-default ports no problem via ONVIF, but not the FI9900, so I knew that the problem is the FI9900p camera, not the utility or my network. I talked to Foscam US tech support and they indicated that ONVIF would be implemented in a firmware update in about 1 month (say early October).  I was about to give up, but then today I saw the review by Alex noting that he had got Synology SS to connect to the FI9900P using the ONVIF default port 888, so I changed the ONVIF port back to the default of 888 and gave it a try - success! So it looks like ONVIF support is in fact in place in the FI9900P, but may have some bugs such as currently only working with the default port 888. However that's a good start, and with communications established I can now try out the logging and recording on the Synology SS.  A few more tips / observations:  1) For daylight savings time (DST) you still need to set the offset to 30 so as to get a 60 minute delta in your camera time, not set to 60 like you would expect. This applies to many Foscam (and other China- sourced) current IP cameras. I don't understand the rationale, but at least I can make it work and get the correct time.  2) The HDR video setting seemed to make things worse (picture very dark rather than better, so I left it off.  3) Some of the documentation in the HIKVISION Network Camera User Manual v5.1.0, and downloadable from their site, is quite pertinent to Foscam cameras, and much more detailed and explanatory (such as the explanation around password validity, DST setting, video settings, etc.)  4) for future IP camera acquisition I am going to look more closely at HIKVISION and Dashua as alternatives to Foscam.  Hope this helps others.

review_body:
Bought directly from Foscam. It works, but it is huge and the amount of signal increase seems minimal.

Also, since it is heavy and long, the joint in the antenna is not strong enough to effectively keep it where you point it.

If you have a rebooting problem with your camera and think it may be due to low signal, before you but this, read on. I bought this because I moved a camera to a new location and was having reboot problem (when a Foscam camera loses connection with the network, it reboots). This antenna did not solve the issue. I swapped out another of my Foscams and that one had the same issue.

I late found out that some of the older Foscams have a reboot issue when facing a bright outdoor scene (like trees in the sun). My cameras that had been performing perfectly inside for over a year would not work at all when they got a view out a window.

I would check that issue before assuming you have a signal problem.

I don't think it is seller fault, as all items were in the sealed plastic. Most probably poor manufacturing. The hole in the plastic housing very small. product_title: LCD Display Screen Repair Part For Nikon Coolpix S8200 Sony HX50 HX50V HX300 Without Blacklight New
review_body: If you are buying this part for a SONY CYBERSHOT DSC HX-300... STOP!!!  I had cracked my screen and needed to replace it.  The seller shipped this part quickly and it was in good condition, but it doesn't work properly on my camera.  The manufacturer claims that it fits several different cameras---which it does---and it does fit the HX-300 just fine.  The problem: the LCD doesn't let the light through, so that even though the backlight is working fine and is super bright, when it's all put together it's very dark/dim as if there's no backlight at all.  In fact, I can see the menus and I can see what the lens is capturing, but everything is very faint and hard to see.  I tested it without the backlight plugged in, and it was totally dark, which confirmed that the backlight itself is working, but is not the problem.  I spoke to a camera technician who explained that despite the claim the manufacturers make, this replacement screen is NOT compatible with the camera, electronically.  As a result, it's not working right.  He said the only screen he kneows that is compatible with my camera at this point is a "Sony original replacement screen," and he steered me to a site that sells genuine Sony replacement parts: https://sony.emcompass.com/item/9596986/Sony/1-811-762-11/Lcd_Module  I purchased the part and it works like a charm.  Unfortunately, I had to pay $80 instead of $20 :-(  (I'm not even going to try to get a refund...)  Note: on the plastic wrap that came with the screen, there was a label with the number S8200 on it.  Could it be that this screen is actually designed to work with the Nikon S8200---which also has a 3" backlit screen?  Note #2: By the way, there is an awesome video on Youtube with great step-by-step instructions on how to remove the old screen and replace it with the new one.

product_title: Samsung SNH-E6440BN Smartcam Full HD Outdoor LP Camera
review_body:
I have been using this camera for 6 months now and feel qualified to review it.

1. This is an outdoor camera. I have it underneath the eve of the house out of direct rain and sun. Nevertheless the screen fogged up a couple of times and never seemed to clear properly. I now have permanent spot on the image where the picture is blurry at night because the night time LEDs are also behind the same clear cover.

2.
the camera sometimes stops recording events to the SD card. It was not out of space, and I also had overwrite checked. The only way to fix this was to restart it. There is no remote restart so I have to go and physically unplug it to restart, another poor design non feature.

3.
I just reformatted the SD card while it was in the unit (note this is an SD card that has been in there for months recording events) and once it finished it no longer recognised the SD card. I likely have to take it out and format FAT in my PC to make it work. Yes I did restart it.

4.
The biggest fault of all is the fact that I have to use Samsung servers to retrieve recorded events from the SD card. This actually would be ok if it worked. Most of the time it fails to connect or "loses connection" half way through playback. If you are thinking that this is because I have a bad network that is not so. My camera is on a LAN ( I tried wireless and everything was worse when accessing the camera on WiFi) Both inside my home and out on a cell network the camera access is flaky and not reliable at all and is soo slow. Mush of the time the system says the servers are down or are going down for maintenance. This would be ok since its free IF they gave another option for retrieving the event recordings.

5. This camera needs a way to directly retrieve the SD recorded events and download them to my PC without using the unreliable Samsung server.
Samsung could you please add the features asked for above.

review_body: These are technically very good cameras.  There seem to be about 10 different camera brands all using the same construct.  The weakness of this product is the firmware and software.  Even the P2P doesn't work very well.  I had to run it 3 times to get both cameras to actually connect.  The browser plugin for the cloud viewer lacks all the usable features of the mobile software.  Sadly, as soon as you leave the WiFi connection with your mobile device, it no longer connects through the web.  You have to switch to port-forwarding and reset your cameras to use a static IP address so it doesn't keep disconnecting.  If you use Port forwarding, P2P no longer works.  Port Forwarding can also corrupt your router settings, particularly if you have more than 1 camera.  It shouldn't be this difficult to use these cameras.  The software should be able to either install these properly without intensive intervention, but that's still a dream at this point.  Documentation is useless.  And forget calling the help line or trying to use the included remote installation card from Foscam.  Average wait time on hold is more than an hour.  Great software / app opportunity here for someone to develop and exploit this weakness.  Bracket design doesn't space camera far enough from wall to allow space for antenna.  Needs to have both adjustable distance from wall and provide at least 1/2 inch more space.

review_body: I wanted a better portrait lens for my Sony A7ii without breaking the bank, was able to pick this up for a fraction of the price. I have not used manual lenses before, ever. I've had this lens for about 3 months now and I absolutely love it. I have an a-mount with a fairly cheap dummy adapter that works perfectly with my camera. I am able to take amazing shots, even in low light, that I was never able to do with the kit lens. I actually dread using the kit lens now, and have considered just getting rid of it and getting a smaller focal length prime Rokinon to replace it, as this 85mm you have to stand a considerable distance away from the subject to get a full body shot. I primarily take pictures of people at conventions and it does pose a problem with an 85mm prime, but if you want amazing portraits without breaking the bank this is the lens for you. I was skeptical at first about using a manual lens, but after figuring out the aperture ring, focus zoom, and the focus peaking I feel as though I'm not losing any time by not having autofocus. I will be in the market for another smaller focal length lens from Rokinon to add to my photography collection.

product_title: XVIM 8 Channel H.264 Recording DVR Surveillance Kit with 8 x 900TVL Indoor/Outdoor Night Vision IR-Cut Weatherproof Cameras
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:caf452f90963be5f8b36fbe3de3eda04]] ✏️ Quick thoughts to supplement my video demonstration.

Everything you need is included except for a monitor (one that accepts either HDMI or VGA) and a hard drive (just a basic laptop hard drive, \\"SATA\\" like this one: [[ASIN:B00AAKF8KC Generic 320 GB 320GB 2.5 Inch Sata Laptop Internal Hard drive 5400 RPM For Laptop/Mac/PS3 (320 GB)]].

I like this security system because:
- It's very easy to setup. Yes it takes a while (lots of steps) but it's relatively easy compared to other systems.
- There are a ton of features--everything from motion detection (which works wonderful) to an email alert system when it detects something (you have to be hooked up to a wired network of course). You can also schedule out when exactly you want it to record (e.g. after business hours).
- Easy navigation: Just need a mouse (included). Click around and right click to \\"go back\\" in the navigation.
- Very smooth, excellent quality footage. Not like that choppy stuff you see on old CCTV security systems.
- Tons of long cables. 60 foot cables (8 of them!). Note: Due to the length of the cable, there's a slight 1 second delay from the event to when you see it on your monitor.
- Full metal, tough camera design.
- Awesome in low-light/darkness. Infrared lights work wonderfully to light up the room when it's dark. (of course the human eye can't see infrared, but it lights up enough for the camera to film everything)
- Incredibly good price here on Amazon. Just factor in a hard drive and a monitor.

Overall I am very impressed with this camera system. An excellent bang for your buck, especially considering how many cameras they give you.

I was given a sample of this product in exchange for a review and demonstration. Hope demonstration and test helps!

📍 Bottom line: would I recommend this product to one of my friends?
👍 Yes, absolutely.

product_title: Meade Instruments LightSwitch Series Telescope
review_body:
Amazing telescope!

Main reasons why:

- FULLY automated! Literally, you just flip a switch and a few minutes later, it is aligned. Then, all you do is pick an object and it slews automatically to that object. Does not get any easier.

- Audio/video explanation of what you are observing. For me, this is critical. I am a beginner, and hearing interesting facts about what I am observing is really interested and makes me enjoy what I am looking at.

- Very small! The Schmidt-Cassegrain design is a fraction of the size of a regular, full-size 6" scope (Dob, for example). Super portable, but very powerful. It is great to have such a small scope that performs as well as a much larger one.

- Build quality. Really feels solid and performs the same.

Overall, GREAT performer, super easy to use, tons of technology built-in, and allows you to maximize the time you observe without fussing over alignment, etc.

review_body:
really really wanted this to work. I received this yesterday to use in my business. My husband tried to install it on our wifi at the shop. He got it to the point of inserting the sd card. Everything seemed to be fine. We were still connected with the cord to the router and it worked. Then he tries to put the SD card in. I don't think he's use to working with the smaller sd cards and had a very difficult time putting it in. He finally got it to read the card, but then the internet connection would go out. If he took the card out, he would get the internet back. This went on for a few hours trying to figure this out. The still shots were what I really bought this camera for. I'm not going to sit around and watch who comes to the door (inside) 24/7. I wanted to see who was going in and out of my shop or if my boxes as been picked up and so forth. He never could seem to get the sd card to work AND the internet connection. Really strange.

Fast foward..... it is the next morning and I decided to try from scratch to install this camera in my home. I figure my husband must have been doing something wrong. We are not amateurs with electronic devices and I really couldn't figure out why he was having such difficulty over at my shop. I plugged in the ac adapter to an outlet and then plugged the ethernet cord into my router. The vimtag is on because of the red light on the right side. But it is not even connecting to my internet here at the house at all. No green lights.... nothing. I've waited about 3 minutes inbetween tries and nothing.

So needless to say I am VERY disappointed with this product. Not sure if we just got a defective one or not, but I find it really, really strange that both my husband (over at my shop) and myself here at home cannot get this thing to work for various reasons. Like I said before, this is not our first rodeo with electronic devices but after a quick call to the company, I plan on returning this product. Does anyone know of another similar product for us to try. We really need the still shots to be captures but I'm not seeing that features on any of the other cameras like this.

product_title: GoPro Camera HERO+ LCD HD Video Recording Camera
review_body:
I bought two of the new Hero+ LCD cameras to replace my aging Hero HDs that I use on my vintage Formula Vee race car. The performance of the new cameras is very good, I'm now shooting my footage at 1080p 60fps and over the last two race weekends had zero issues with dropped frames and the picture quality is a big improvement over my old Heros.

One thing I didn't realize when I ordered these was that they are sealed units, you can't replace the battery or replace the external casing, the camera is permanently mounted within the protective housing. If I had known I might have popped for the next model up, since it is easy to get a scratch on the protective case cover in auto racing (lots of stuff gets thrown about on a racetrack!) and it's a lot more economical to replace a $15 housing than a $299 camera. I should have read the product descriptions more closely.

Also the battery life of the Hero+ LCD is about half of that of my old Hero HDs, and I learned that the hard way when we had three races in one day and I didn't even think to check the battery levels (which had started the day fully charged) but then found that both cameras had died half-way through the third race. My old Heros would make it through an entire race weekend without needing a recharge (and I had extra batteries just in case, not possible with the new model).

But now that I know that I can use a portable USB charger to top off the cameras between races so they're always 100%, just an extra step I never had to worry about before. For the money I'm very happy with the picture quality so hopefully the housings will last the life of the cameras themselves and be a non-issue.

But them reaching out to do an exchange is worth something.  Also, it seems that TriVision, Sharx, and Phylink all use the same software. Customer support was responsive to the issues via email, but couldn't offer solutions other than those already in the manual.  It is unfortunate that such horrible software ruins the user experience for a really good piece of hardware.

review_body: Action cameras market is filled with all kind of accessories and new little gadgets. But no one made a compact size case shaped for GoPro like Shineda able to carry up to 2 GoPro cameras inside. Fine ends and attractive colors create a natural space for your action camera and all the accessories you might think of. The Shineda Grid Case is foam cut-out system to take all your GoPro accessories inside: A GoPro plus case, SD cards cut-out, remote cut-out, and a double space cut-out for carrying large gear amongst others. The foam inside is PET to keep this way the case undeformable. When you open the Shineda Grid Case you'll see a grey flap on the left compartment which you can move.  Once you've done this you will find a new full bungeed section to carry more gear such as cables, your charger, thumbscrews, flat adhesive mounts, spare batteries, quick release buckle, etc. In case you wanted to carry even more gear, you can always remove the bungeed section on the left flap and that way you can create more space. The Grid Case can resist water but it is important to understand this: light rain or water splash so don't dive it. Made of EVA: Ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) an extremely elastic material that can be sintered to form a porous material similar to rubber, yet with excellent toughness. As they mention, the Grid Case is the only case with 3 neoprene pockets for filters, that a great plus and thumbs up for the company! The Grid Case is a so well organized case that will make your life easier once out there.

review_body:
Added 2/15/2016 because of confusion:

FYI One star because 2/3 of the cameras on Amazon are currently Gray market with hacked firmware. If you get an international version of this camera (or buy from a reputable Hikvision retailer) I rate it 4 stars.

Original Review:
Beware of the gray market Hikvision cameras that are actually the Chinese version with English firmware updated. I tried to download the latest official firmware from Hikvision and load it, bricked all of the cameras. Then I found out that most of the cameras being sold are gray market, not us or international editions. Only those official editions support the official hikvision USA firmware.

Apparently, two ways to identify the "proper" cameras that get official firmware updates are either:

1)Red/White box (if you get the camera shipped in a brown box, it's very likely that it's Chinese).
2) If the serial number contains CCCH then you've gotten a gray market version. CCWR should be updatable from Hikvisions official firmware sources.

There is a whole community devoted to hacking the cheaper Chinese versions of these cameras, but I couldn't make it go in a few hours and I'm a pretty knowledgeable person. Good luck, the camera is fine, but get one that supports the official firmware & gets upgrades!

product_title: Deecam D200 Wireless IP/Network Security HD 720P Surveillance Camera Pan & Tilt with Two-Way Audio, Day/Night
review_body:
The Deecam D200 (aka Tenvis TH661) is a network-attached camera. The box contains the following:
• The camera
• Ethernet (network) cable
• Power adapter
• Mounting bracket, with screws and wall plugs
• Software CD (Mini CD)
• Manual

The camera housing is made of shiny black plastic but it feels nicely weighted and solid. There's a wifi antenna on the back (it doesn't appear to be replaceable, unfortunately), a Micro SD/SDHC card slot (documentation claims that cards up to 32GB are supported - I had no problems using a 32GB card), an Ethernet port and a socket for the power adapter. The manual is surprisingly good - it covers the initial setup steps clearly. The manual and provided software is also available online (see below).

Setup is straightforward. I connected it to my wired network and it found an IP address within a few seconds. I did initial setup using the Life Online app on my iPhone but it's also possible to use the Tenvis app (available for Apple iOS and Android). The camera supports both wired and wireless connections - the wireless worked fine for me (2.4GHz only) but I prefer using the wired connection for performance/stability reasons. Connectivity to your wireless network can be setup using the app.

In addition to managing the camera using a mobile app, there is also a web interface - just browse to the IP address that the camera is on and log in with your administrator username and password. The web interface allows you to configure far more options than the mobile app. For example, it allows for some advanced functions like triggering an ftp upload of a photo/video or email from an alert, which is very useful. If you're unsure of the address of your camera, you can use the provided Tenvis Search Tool, which will find it automatically (this works for Windows and Mac). You can also view the camera feed from the web interface and I had no problem accessing it from a Mac.

In use, I'm very impressed with this camera. The image quality is excellent, both during the day and at night, and maximum resolution is 1280x720 (ie 720p). Setting up alerts (to record when movement is detected) is very easy and works well but you will need to provide an SD/SDHC card to record to the camera itself. Another thing I like is that it's easy to move the camera (tilt and pan) remotely. Unfortunately movement below the horizontal is limited, so if you're not using the bracket, don't mount it too high up otherwise you won't be able to see too far below the camera's position. But that's a minor criticism, really.

The camera has a built-in microphone and can record audio. I can also be used for two way communication but I found it a bit clunky as you need to switch modes in the app from listening to speaking each time you want to say something and then hear the response.

Note: Disable the UPnP and P2P settings on the camera or make sure the appropriate ports are blocked on your router so that your camera is not accessible from the Internet. In the past some models of Tenvis cameras have had security problems (just search online for "Tenvis security hole") so you *do not* want these cameras exposed to the Internet.

Pros:
+ Easy to set up
+ Very good image quality, both during the day and at night
+ Excellent functionality
+ Fully-featured web interface

Cons:
- Limited movement below the horizontal
- Two-way audio a bit clunky
- Very important: make sure you disable the UPnP/P2P functionality

As mentioned, the camera itself is actually made by Tenvis - you can download the manuals and additional software online (just search for "Tenvis D200" or "Tenvis TH661" for this particular model).

Overall, I'm very impressed with this camera. It offers a lot of features for the money - for under $60, it's a bargain. Highly recommended. Note -this camera may be available from a few sellers, so make sure you price compare before buying!may be available from a few sellers, so make sure you price compare before buying!

product_title: ImogenStudio QCP-A200 +Cam Pro Video Security Accessory
review_body: When I first opened my package from Amazon I noticed that my “brand new” ImogenStudio QCP-A200 had been opened. The sticker-seals on the box were pulled off.  I continued to pull out the cam and all of the other parts and started the process of setting it up. It is very simple as long as you follow the instructions completely. It’s a quick 4 or 5 step process. Just make sure that when you connect the cam to your phone at the end of the process, that the cam is in the “off” position. It seems weird but it is what you’re supposed to do.  I really do like having the cam. I will be using it as a baby monitor. It has decent resolution.  The day vision is in color and the night vision is black and white. I included a picture of what the night vision looks like in my son's room. The microphone on the cam is really pretty good and the speaker works well also. I love that I can be at work and watch my son at naptime. I can record the cam's view on my phone and the cam records any motion that it picks up. There are only a few things that I would put into the “cons” list: 1) there is a bit of a delay in the video feed and if there’s any lag in your wifi, that doesn’t help either, 2) there’s also a delay in the audio, 3) the biggest problem is that the day vision does not toggle back over once the camera is in night mode. You have to point the camera at a light for a second or cover the lens and then uncover it for the lens to go back into day mode. Those things in mind, I did buy a second one for my mom to be able to monitor my grandmother while nurses are caring her for.

product_title: Foscam 2 Megapixel Network Camera - Color FI9900P
review_body:
I purchased this camera to work along with a Synology Surveillance station (up to date in version 7.0).

After HOURS (litterally) of tweaking, I FINALLY have reached a point where it is all working fine.

1. 1080p mode has stutter issue. Every 0.5s or so. It's not an issue with the NAS, it is within the camera itself. I tested the camera recording into an FTP server, the recorded files themselves had the stutter issue. I haven't tried SD card recording, but that is pointless for my application.
That's unacceptable and at the same time, I found that 720p mode was not just in par with the full HD mode, but actually *superior* in terms of image quality. The lack of definition is not noticeable, as the compression is so hard. On the other hand the 720p mode is visibly smoother (not just the 30FPS vs. 25FPS) and somewhat sharper in my findings.

So, in my testing, the best image quality is reached with 720p mode in 30FPS. Haven't noticed any difference between VBR or CBR, but I chose 4M bitrate either way (highest setting).

2. You MUST reboot the camera when playing with the different video modes. I almost drove myself crazy because the NAS couldn't write the 720p files, the recordings were corrupted, while the 1080p were recorded just fine. I had a really HARD time repeating what I was seing, playing with the settings back and forth, until I decided I should reboot. Bingo. 720p files were properly recorded too. And the recorded files are butter-smooth, no stutter. Sharp, and smooth, unless in low light, movements can get blurred but that is to be expected.

3. I had then constant "connection lost" "connection recovered" messages in Synology SS. Almost drove me crazy too I must say. I thought the wifi range was the culpit, but no. Until I fund online I should set the camera in SS settings in "UDP" protocol instead of "TCP". Solved it immediately.

I have no long term view but so far so good. Connection seems to be solid, recordings are good and stutter-free.

Last but not least, the image quality is excellent. Night vision is good too.

I just regret that 1080p mode is marketing BS. The bitrate is compressing too hard, destroying any details that all those pixels might have captured. And, the camera struggles to keep up with the video feed, stuttering every half a second or so.

Camera is quite fast to reboot.

Interface is rather clear and fast. I did not find it overly buggy either.

Connection is through port 88 and NOT 80 as one would expect. Lost 30 min figuring that out.

I made it work in Synology SS using "Generic ONVIF" with port 888 (not 88 this time). Only H.264 is available.

Hope this helps.
