product_title: Vstarcam HD Home Wireless/WiFi 720P IP Camera Onvif P2P Pan/Tilt Micro SD Card Slot Audio & Microphone
review_body:
I don't even know where to begin. Make sure you set your expectations before you buy. All I wanted was an indoor camera with pan/tilt/zoom and audio so I could watch and listen from a PC in another room. I suppose I got that so I can't complain too much. If I'd paid more I would give this thing 1 star. But, I paid about $50 so I'm trying very hard to keep that in mind. I WANT to give it 2 stars... but I'm going to give it 3 because it does what I wanted and it was cheap. That said...

Appearance of product - cheapish, never survive outside, no where near waterproof. I mention this because one of the answers to a question suggests it it suitable for an outdoor installation.

Packaging - OK

Condition of arrival - OK

Quality of Instructions included - Poor. Highly focused on getting you to download an app which does little to walk you through the setup of the camera. It makes it seem you can just plug it in and connect. Nope, you need to connected to a wired network to get on the camera and set the wireless password. I knew that but the instructions do little to explain that. I set mine to a static IP then connected it to my wireless. Not a big deal for me but I can see it leaving some people very lost trying to figure it out.

The mac address is not on the outside of the camera. So don't think you will look at your arp table, find the mac, then the DHCP IP assigned to it and access the camera. You'll either have to guess about, look for the newest lease or use the "find your camera" software they offer to locate the camera so you can assign and IP address to it if needed.

Quality of website - Poor. Tells you very little actual useful information. Also, I had a lot of difficulty reaching the website from the U.S. It kept timing out and was very very slow to load anything.

Quality of software.
PC Eye4 Software. Cryptic at best. Requires you to create an account with Eye4 to even use it. I find that intrusive, I see no way to use the software "offline" if I wished. But, more than that it took me 6 tries to create an account as I kept getting an unknown error when I tried. Also, every time I start the software it tells me "There is no disk in the drive. Please insert a disk into drive F:" I have no idea what that means except maybe it's scanning my drives. I'm not so convinced this software isn't malware more than video software. When I click "Continue" I get a Login screen not in English (I did choose English when installing) and I have to enter that account information I was forced to create.
Actually using the software... well I got the camera connected and I can monitor it, pan and tilt etc... it's poorly written, amateurish in appearance and function. While I figure most of it out, I cannot get the audio to work all the time. Just nothing, turn on/off whatever, no audio. Close the software, login again and I have audio, not great but I have it. There is no noise cancelling whatsoever, so you cant have the mic and speakers on at the same time. You'll get nothing but a feedback loop.

The software they give to locate the camera on the network, it worked OK. I'd have to say it's about the best the have going for them. It finds the camera quickly so you can get the IP etc...

The android software is dreadful. Video lags badly, audio cuts in and out and gets out of sync, pan/tilt is slow to respond and zoom does not work. I'm using an HTC M One 9. It has plenty of power and memory to do the job, it's just a poor app.

Recording. So far, I do know you cannot set it to record on motion. You can set it to alarm and record on motion or record on a schedule. I would like record when there is motion, that's all. No annoying alarm sounds, just record when things are moving, don't record when they are not and do that 24/7. I can't find anyway to make that happen. It wants to blare outa siren sound. Maybe I'm missing a setting, but so far no luck motion = make annoying siren sound.

product_title: Kodak CFH-V15 - HD WiFi Video Monitoring Surveillance Security Camera, Pan/Tilt, Two-Way Audio, Night Vision & Free Cloud Storage
review_body:
In a line - this is a good camera for entry level-ip camera users but not a good camera for those with other ip cameras.

The good - the camera just works. You plug it in, set up the app to connect to wifi and you're off operating the camera. The picture quality is good and it does what it's supposed to do. I didn't really play with the 24 hour storage feature although I think the free storage may be useful to some users.

The bad - The software is not particularly robust and a little laggy. Even scrolling seems difficult although pinch to zoom worked well. The only way to access the controls of the camera is through the kodak app. There is no web based access. It also appears incompatible with other ip camera software. This is a major problem if you already have non-kodak ip cams like foscams. Finally, and perhaps most importantly, this camera is a bandwidth hog! We have a solid cable connection and an ac wireless router. I was getting video streaming lag after installing the camera. Checked the router and found the Kodak camera was eating up bandwidth like a champ.

Conclusion - I'd recommend this camera to non-technical users that had bandwidth to spare. If they were heavy netflix users, gamers, or had a set of existing Foscams, I would recommend they go with a different ip cam, like a Foscam, that would give them more flexibility usually at a lower price.

I purchased this WiFi camera to use primarily as a baby monitor. After our little one has moved out of the crib I intended to use it for home security and monitoring.

The sharpness isn't tack sharp when wide open, and when you stop it down it gets a swirly effect due to the imprecise/irregularly closing aperture blades.  All this may sound bad, but it is a cool effect and you can't get this look with the ultra precise computer engineered lenses found on most modern cameras. This will not work well on full frame because the full circle of black vignette would reduce the visible part of the frame to about 30% of full. product_title: Mcoplus MK-A7II a72 Pro Built-in 2.4g Wireless Control Vertical Battery Grip for Sony A7 2 ii as Sony VG-C2EM
review_body:
Product arrived on time and the grip itself works as promised. I had owned a Sony branded grip for the Sony A7s and this grip for the A7R II feels every bit as solid as the Sony grip.

For those considering getting a grip for your Sony. I highly recommend it for two reasons. The obvious one is that it doubles the battery life without having to swap batteries - a big plus when shooting video or time lapse. The second reason is that if you mount the A7 series to a tripod you no longer have access to the battery compartment, forcing you to detach it from the tripod. When shooting timelapse this is a deal breaker. With a battery grip attached you'll have side access to the batteries, meaning you won't have to remove the camera from the tripod to access the batteries.

One difference with this third-party grip vs the Sony grip is that the Sony grip has a door that opens (stays attached to camera) and you slide out the dual battery tray, whereas with this grip the end slides out and is attached to the battery tray. I prefer this method over Sony's as the end piece gives you something to hold on to while swapping batteries - and actually feels less fragile compared to Sony's slide out tray.

I have not tested the remote control. It looks to have timelapse functionality along with the standard remote trigger, but I won't have a chance to test it (no AAA batteries) until tomorrow or Sunday. If it doesn't work then I'll reduce my rating to 4 stars, but I have no reason to believe that it wouldn't work.

When attaching a grip to the A7 series you need to remove the battery door of the camera. Sony makes it easy to do this - just slide a small switch on the door and pop it off. Instead of worrying about losing this little piece of plastic these battery grips (third party and Sony model) have a spot where you can attach the battery door, so that it's always with you for those times you decide to remove the grip.

product_title: Leviton 5350-PT4 RJ11 Surge Protector
review_body:
This product can be installed in the Leviton 51120 PTC surge protection panel or directly into a wall outlet. We have only used them in conjunction with the Leviton 51120 PTC which is installed in our electrical and communications equipment room. The 51120 is tied directly into the main electrical panel ground bus but can be installed on a branch panel or plugged into an outlet as well. We have been using these 5350 units for at least 10 years and I will give them a 4 out or 5. We live in the south and on the coast so consequently have some extreme storms with lots of lightning.

We have replaced these devices at least 7-8 times as they have functioned as advertised and faulted out and thus protected the down stream equipment. We did have a recent extreme lightning strike that either hit the house of within feet and the 5350 unit and the phone wires attached were melted and current did get through and burned up a 4-1 fax, printer, scanner copier that was attached to the line as well as a wall telephone, DSL modem and other items. This was obviously extreme so likely nothing would have protected from this strike. I have had numerous other events where lightning struck the ground or close by and the device functioned properly destroying itself but protecting the downstream equipment.

product_title: YONGNUO YN622N-KIT Wireless i-TTL Flash Trigger Kit with LED Screen for Nikon including 1X YN622N-TX Controller and 1X YN622 N Transceiver
review_body:
I really wanted to like this product, and have been waiting to purchase it for a while. In my opinion, it has the best interface and features of anything else on the market, at any price. The display is great, the build quality is very good, easy to use, and the super sync works well.

I really needed a TTL capable remote, but unfortunately TTL is the one area this product just plain doesn't work. It seems Yongnuo hasn't been able to figure out the secret sauce in Nikon's latest i-TTL protocols, at least not for all products. I know some have said it works with the D750, but I'm wondering how closely they tested it. Yes, it works and will fire, but is not accurate in TTL. I tested in a controlled setting with no ambient light so I could see what the flash was doing. It may be harder to spot if you're using outdoors with plenty of ambient mixed in.

When used with my D750, I get wildly inconsistent TTL exposures from frame to frame, and the ones that are close, are still about 1 stop underexposed compared to CLS TTL. I always made sure to wait several seconds between frames to make sure the flash is not just out of power, but strangely enough, it's usually the first frame that is the darkest. I feel like it is flashing a tad too early before the sensor is exposed. I can see the flash fire in the viewfinder before the mirror clicks up.

Switch to manual mode, and it works flawlessly. However, I already own a set of $30 manual YN-603s, and as nice as it would be to have manual remote control of power, it's just not worth $80 when TTL isn't useable. I have also noticed a strange warm color cast on some frames when using the triggers, probably due to it dumping a bit too early, which may also be the cause of the underexposure inconsistency.

I spent hours testing these things and found some interesting facts... My Nikkor 50 1.8G actually works perfect in TTL mode, however my Nikkor 16-35 f4G and my Tamron 70-200 2.8 VC are inconsistent in TTL. Using an SB-700 flash for all. All lenses are perfect in manual. It seems that the 622n TX just can't fully understand the information coming from the D750. I updated the triggers to the newest firmware 1.06 and still no luck. There have also been strange issues with it occasionally getting "stuck" where it would fire at full power no matter what, even after double checking the settings. The only way to fix was to turn the units off and on again.

I wish these would just work, because there is nothing else on the market that fits this need as perfectly as the yn-622n tx does. I'm not going to risk waiting for a firmware fix, so I returned to Amazon while I have the chance.

product_title: PiSector 4G Cellular GSM Wireless Security Alarm System Quad-band Support 2G/3G/4G network
review_body: I am only giving this 4 stars, lest you think this is a "paid review", to get a free sensor.... but at this point (installed for a week), I have no complaints.  I purchased this system to replace a fully wired alarm system that was getting old. The system came with all sensors pre-programmed, so all I had to do was change the sensor names, and alter some of the settings (e.g. delay alarm, emergency sensor, etc.). Testing was fairly easy, and for those that prefer video instructions, there are some available on the PiSector website that are quite complete.  Overall, a very complete package for the price. I also bought a remote keypad, so that the main panel could be placed somewhere that intruders would not find right away. I also purchased an optional smoke alarm. I estimate that it took me about 2 hours to get everything programmed/configured the way I wanted it, including time learning the system operation, reading the manuals, and watching the videos. This is time well-spent; the system is really quite capable, with many possible options, and could be confusing if one has not read the instructions.  To make full use of the event reporting system, you will want to buy a SIM card. I got one from AlarmSIM, a small, family-owned, company. (They seem responsive, but I have not had to deal with them, yet).  So far, I'm pleased with the overall system. I'll update this review, should that change.  The Good: 1. PiSector email response to questions was within 24 hours (they are in a different time-zone   than EDT, because their responses arrive around mid-night). The support was   helpful. 2. Mostly setup out-of-the-box. Just a few programming additions to make it fully   customized. (Full disclosure: I'm an electrical engineer and computer programmer,   so I'm familiar with these sorts of systems...it may be more complicated for people   not used to this sort of thing). 3. Everything comes with batteries pre-installed. 4. The landline calling works as described,and is a nice feature for such   and inexpensive system. 5. The GSM system is up-to-date, so when the 2G system gets retired   in 2016, the system will still perform (unlike some of the other systems   I considered before buying this one). 6. All the sensors worked fine, and there are a number of add-on sensors   to extend the system.  The Bad: 1. The system is a bit awkward to program, but this is not done frequently, so I can forgive this little annoyance. 2. As most reviewers have noted, the 3M tape provided does not stick worth a darn. I tested this by installing   a door sensor with it. The next morning, the magnet was on the floor, instead of on the door. Get your own tape,   or use super-glue (which PiSector actually recommends in their FAQ...even they realize the tape sucks.) 3. The system would delay for two minutes after disarming, until I did a "Reset to Factory Defaults", on   the advice of the PiSector support person. Not sure what it was doing, but the "reset" fixed it. I   recommend doing a factory reset right out-of-the box, so that subsequent programming is not lost   if your system arrives in the state mine was in... 4. The instructions are written by someone who speaks English as a second language. The grammar   and syntax are sometimes so awkward that they're funny. This can make deciphering what they're talking   about a bit of a challenge sometimes. 5. The built-in microphone (which is used to record sensor names, and for the intercom), is of very low   quality. The recorded sound is barely understandable, and using the two-way talk (or listen) feature   is difficult unless you get your face right up to the main panel. For about $0.25 they could have sprung   for an op-amp to increase the gain....  The Ugly: 1. The sound/voice indicators are not that loud, and when the main panel is   placed far from the (optional) remote entry keypad, one cannot hear the system status   sounds. One reviewer modified the panel by adding a bluetooth transmitter and   remote speaker to overcome this. While this is clever, it is probably beyond the   abilities of the typical purchaser. The remote keypad does blink, telling you what it   sent the main panel, but it's not clear that the main panel actually did that.... 2. The replacement/extra sensors are expensive. 3. The system does not integrate with video surveillance cameras, nor is it ever   likely to....the company has a lengthy paragraph in their FAQ in which they   say you should just get yourself some internet-enabled cameras if you want   to watch what's going on.

product_title: Nest cam security camera
review_body:
Long-time Dropcam user here. Recently moved into a new apartment, and decided to get a Nest Cam. I ended up returning it though, because Nest removed a few features that were critical for me. Here's my review.

The Good
-Sleek new hardware design
-Similarly sleek new Nest website and iPhone app

The Bad
-Confusing, redundant UI's. There's the new Nest website and iPhone app, and there's also (still) the old Dropcam website and iPhone app. Why both? Finish the transition already! Get rid of the old one. It only causes confusion
-Notifications are unreliable. I setup my new Nest Cam in my living room, waved my arms around like a lunatic, but didn't immediately get a notification on my phone or via e-mail. That's kind of important. I don't want a burglar to have a 10 minute head start.
-Oh, and e-mail notifications... they dropped that feature! Whaaaat, right????
-Another feature they dropped, the one where you could choose to have the camera turn off automatically when you're around. Now, you have to MANUALLY turn it on/off. What year is this? 1992? Ain't nobody got time for that!!

Nest, you made a great piece of hardware, and a great sleek new website and iPhone app, but you RUINED it by removing some critical features, and failing on the simple things (like sending immediate notifications).

product_title: Selfie Stick, EasyAcc 3-In-1 Self-portrait Monopod Extendable Wireless Bluetooth Stick with built-in Bluetooth Remote Shutter with Adjustable Phone Holder for iPhone 6 6S 6Plus, iPhone 5 5s, Samsung Galaxy S6 S5, Android – Black
review_body:
First of all, I would like to thank EasyAcc for sending this product to me for review.

When the EasyAcc Selfie Stick QuickSnap Pro came in, the box was beaten up but the selfie stick did not seem physically damaged. It did not come with a manual (which was strange) but the other accessories such as a micro USB cord and hand strap were included. Next, I tried turning it on (by holding my finger on the shutter button) and no lights turned on. However when I plugged it into the charger, a red light would come on next to the charging port. After 3+ hours of charging, I tried it again and nothing. I contacted EasyAcc and they sent me another one. When it came in, it was the same thing except the new one came with a manual. Then, I contacted Amazon for a replacement and they sent a new one. This time, everything was included and everything works fine. I cannot believe I received two defective products before receiving a working product.

Despite the hassle of trying to get a product that worked, I was still impressed by the device. Initially, I was impressed at its' small, compact size when it is not extended. When fully extended, I do not feel like it is flexing or unstable. The clamp is awesome! I can hold my iPhone 6 Plus with an Otterbox Commuter series case on it. I am one of the few people who actually use the included lanyard because I am constantly worrying about dropping my device. I find that the included lanyard is a good size for me, but I am small. My friends who try using it are unable to and end up not using it. The loop itself is either too small for their hands to fit through, or uncomfortable on their wrists. The grip is made out of rubber and is not slippery. The shutter button acts as the on/pairing button. There is a blue light that flashes when it is pairing mode. After you pair your phone, the light will turn off until you take the picture. To take the picture, just push on the shutter button and the light will flash, acknowledging that you pushed the button. I do not like how there is no way to tell whether the selfie stick is on or not. I get confused and hope that I do not have to re-pair it. Also, there is no battery icon when I pair it to my iPhone. Another thing to note is if you are on a Samsung device and you use a 3rd party keyboard such as google keyboard, you will need to change your keyboard to the stock Samsung keyboard. When I first paired it to my old Samsung Galaxy S3, I received a pop-up to change it to the stock Samsung keyboard because it registered as a bluetooth keyboard. I was annoyed to have to keep changing keyboards.

Since the Selfie Stick is really compact, I can stick it in my pocket. This is really convenient because I don't have to worry about rummaging through my backpack to find my selfie stick. All I have to do is reach into my pocket, stick my phone on it, and bam, its' done. I've taken this out with my friends and it is definitely a hit. Everyone fits into the photos and it's convince makes it even better!

PROS:
compact size
rubber grip
charging time
standby time
clamp fits large devices
study when fully extended
tactile shutter button

CONS:
No way of knowing if it is on
small lanyard
change keyboards (Samsung devices if using 3rd party keyboard app)
defects (two out of three for me)

Overall, I would definitely recommend this product. I do want to advise you to contact EasyAcc or Amazon if you do receive a defective item because both have an amazing customer service.

product_title: SIRUI P-326 6 Section Carbon Fiber Monopod
review_body:
There is very little that one can say about a Monopod, so I will keep this brief. I really had no need for another Monopod, and have never spent $100 bucks on one. But as a professional photographer of many years I have tried many products.I recently tried the SIRUI K 20 ball head. I fell in love! I kept the K 20 for my Dollica Monopod, and ordered the K 30 ball head for my tripod. They (K 30 & K 20 ball heads) are nothing but "Precision Sweet"!

I was so impressed with this product line, that I went ahead and ordered the P-326. I have a slight back problem, so I carry a monopod with me at all times as more of a walking stick. I also ride a MT. Bike daily and use bungecords to secure my gear to the frame of my bike. Since this Monopod has a 15" retracted size it appealed to me. When it arrived I was really impressed with all aspects of it. In another review I read where it was "QUIET". And unlike other Monopods I have had, it dose not "rattle" when you are walking with it. A good thing! It is extremely light weight, and very strong. I have put a lot of my own body weight (not abusing it) on it and it has never slipped or collapsed as some others I've had. It is quick to extend to the height I want and locks into position with very little tightening of the twist locks.

Side Note: I always put a round rubber protector (Like the ones you put on the bottom of a typical walking cane) on the bottom of my Monopods (available at any hardware store) to preserve the factory installed shoe since I use this all the time, and remove it if I have the need to extent the Stainless Steel point for icy or slippery conditions. Just a bit of advice!

Like the SIRUI Ball Heads, this is without a doubt a professional piece of gear, and I believe it is one of the highest quality photo related gear I have ever used. I recommend this product line very, very highly.
Thanks, Shooter Boone.

For this reason I own several great backpacks that I use depending on where I will be shooting or travel. These include a Lowepro Flipside 300, a Sony alpha LCSBP2, and a Sony carrying bag. I am VERY picky about backpacks. I received my Case Logic SLRC-206 yesterday and I am really impressed. I was looking for a backpack that not only could carry safely my camera gear but also my iPad or 15 inch Laptop. This backpack has the best functional design I ever seen. The materials are very nice, very well padded inside, great use of space and looks very nice. I totally recommend it, it's very hard to find a backpack like this one.

I give it only four stars because the lens hood of the lens attached to the camera keeps getting stuck in the SLR-Suspension System when I pull the camera out. You have to pull it slow and nicely in order to keep the hood attached.

Another reason for the four stars is that I didn't find the straps to be as comfortable as my other backpacks. These are just Ok.

These are just a couple of minor problems for an excellent backpack that, again, I highly recommend.

review_body:
Purchased this 72" Monopod for $15 from ECost and fulfilled by Amazon. I was expecting junk due to the low cost but I now see that it is a great buy! It actually comes in a retail box instead of wrapped in a gob of plastic like most stuff you get on Amazon nowadays. I like that. My first impressions are real good about this.

PROS:
1. Good quality construction. Everything fits tightly.
2. Nice and Sturdy. Very little flex in the tubes when fully extended. Various components all seem to be of a heavy enough gauge.to take normal wear and tear.
3. Nice foam grip!
4. Great 72" height for us tall folk!
5. Easily can handle a medium weight DSLR. No problemo!

CONS:
1. A lot of the construction is plastic so it will fail sooner or later but the gauge is heavy so it will probably take a beating okay.
2. The D-ring on the quick release head is small and difficult to access for us folk with big fingers.
3. Found just one REAL FLAW in the construction though. It is where the head attaches to the metal leg tube . This held together with just ONE tiny self-tapping screw. (see photo) Totally inadequate! And to add insult to injury the person in China who assembled it placed the screw too high on the sleeve and missed the metal leg! The head just falls off! A 'normal' person would probably send it back as defective but I can fix that easy with some epoxy and 2 screws properly set in the head/leg joint. An elephant won't be able to pull it apart when I'm finished! LOL I would give it 5 stars except for this one fault.

SUMMARY: I really like this monopod! I'm sure it will work just fine. I could break it if I wanted to but I'd have to work at it. OH! For you that wonder about the spike tip ... you can rotate the rubber boot down to cover it ... so your Linoleum floors are safe!

review_body:
I can tell you this telescope is great. assembly was easy and parts were prefabbed to excellent quality standards. the finder works okay but I would like a 90 degree viewer finder so I dont have to bend down and stick my head to the scope.
Know that you are not done spending money! Look up eyepiece prices they are ASTRONOMICAL! I bought used and new ones on eBay for a reasonable prices $25-$50 each for cheapest ones you will at least want to buy a 15 mm and a 40 mm and a 2x Barlow eyepiece. 1.25'' sizes are cheapest . you can buy individual 2'' pieces from the Celestron eyepiece kit that is sold on amazon for $270 for $45 a piece separately if you can find them on eBay that's like the cheapest for 2" if you want to go that route . Filters are $15 a piece and up. So do your research on eyepieces. you may be better off buying a kit than separate pieces sometimes.
No camera pictures from this look as clear as the objects seen with your eye in the eyepiece by the way. But it seems like a great beginner scope. One thing tho NO EYEPIECE HOLDER! it has holes for it but doesn't come with it. Why not!
I have a 3d printer so can make one that is on thing averse ( look up Orion eyepiece holder).

30 minute build time. comes with all tools. Use your own Allen wrenches because theirs strip.

product_title: DSTE Pro D-BG4 Vertical Battery Grip for Pentax K-7 K-5 K-5ii K-5iis Digital Camera as D-LI90
review_body:
Great Expectations!

No, that really is a lie actually. Mine were quite tepid as far as my excitement, and expectations. They say you get what you pay for. I say it to all my friends, and family alike. Everything without exception is built to a cost. Commodities work this way. Remember Routers used to cost over $500.00?? Yes you do. I know I did. Along with that MCSE degree you needed to interface it. Well, now they are plug and play for less $50.00.

This one grip is kind of like that. Except it will NOT have the Weather seals of the Factory OEM unit by Pentax. Please know this going in, and all is right with the world. With all the major food groups covered here such as shutter release, locking collar, AF, and more, others state what magic soup buttons come with here. I wanted to share that I am a big person on Ergos, and this grip solves one big gripe for me on what is the best camera I have ever bought.

The Pentax K-5 ii. With my Gorilla sized hands, this is not a DSLR camera, but a small bridge camera with a glandular problem.

Sure it is wide enough, but tall is not in the cards on the K-5 ii. So my small finger has no where to go.

This grip gives me the finger.

Well, that is, it gives my little finger a proper purchase to land on. On top of this, this made in China device feels solid in the hand, fits the K-5 ii a treat. Almost really does look like it belongs on the camera. My mantra on great pictures is the basics, and yes, that camera better fit your hand, and this battery grip by DSTE fills my hand with camera in such a great way. Button feel is average, a bit mushy in actuation, and will not in any way displace the factory grip, I know, I played with one, and just could never swallow that "are you nuts price." Yes, you can now get them for $120.00 or so. I got mine here, this DTSE for $36.00 to my door!

The rotary dials for Shutter, and Aperture are bit chinzy in feel, inthat they don't have that nice release, detent feel of the real deal. Okay now that all the carping about the real deal, and all is out of the way, will it work? Heck yes! My camera functions just fine with Auto Battery detection of all modes, AA Battery, In Body, and In Grip just fine thank you.

So really should you buy the Factory Grip? Now that is really why you are reading this and other reviews here right? Of course it is. I did the same thing, and thought, okay, no downpours of rain, snow, sleet in the cards for this camera. Could I spend the money more wisely, and invest on what I saved on another lens or something? You bet! I did, I have a Sigma on the way ordered today!

Now if you do have weather, and beat your camera up, don't waste your money here, and go buy the original Factory OEM Pentax Grip, do not look back, do not pass GO, and do NOT collect $200.00. You will have a more robust Grip no doubt. Better button actuation, better feeling control dials, and the weather seals too. For me, and I have a feeling many others, this DSTE Battery Grip will do just fine. Even if it dies in 2 years, I got my money's worth. Crazy huh?? Commodities work that way too. They die, you just go buy another one. Like a Router, this will work a treat till it breaks something, and you buy another. Welcome to the value cycle. Now lets go take some pictures. V.C.

The first camera connected to my network immediately and continues to work flawlessly.  Unfortunately, however, the second camera died within two days of installation.  In addition, it constantly lost its connection to my network during the two days that it was working.  I figured this was an aberration so, after returning the second camera, I placed an order for two more (the captioned "twin pack").  To my great disappointment, one of these cameras died in the exact same fashion as the second camera in the first order did (failed to stay connected to the network and then just eventually died).  Thus, out of four cameras, only two worked properly.  Sorry, but a 50% failure rate after two days of use each is just pathetic.  The only upside is that the cameras that did work (the other two), work quite well.  I guess it is possible that I received a bad batch but I certainly will not risk getting another one.  I ended up returning these two and will just stick with the original single camera and cut my losses.  In my humble opinion this company has a real quality control problem.

product_title: Celestron 21035 70mm Travel Scope
review_body: Since being a child I can always remember wanting a telescope. I was so excited when I came across this one as it was finally my opportunity to have one. With all the different types and brands it sure made choosing one rather difficult. I am so glad I got this one. The travel scope and accessories all come packed so beautifully and neatly in the travel case. The travel case is the first thing you notice, when you open the box, and it's extremely nice and made of very good quality with a thick zipper (which is a great thing). The travel scope comes with several different lenses, a cleaning cloth, a CD, and a tripod. My husband and I have a 4 year old and this was the perfect size for not just us but him, he really loved it! We live in a pretty well lit town and my husband was worried about seeing the stars due to how lit everything was around us. This travel scope provided no problems for us when it came to seeing the beautiful stars. It images of the stars were very clear and bright! It was also easy enough to use and interchange lenses that our son was able to do it, after being shown a few times. We also loved how easily we could pack it up and take it to our lake home. The CD provided tons of helpful information and printable sky maps, which really came in handy for helping us as we looked at the sky through the travel scope. If your in the market for a telescope I highly recommend this travel scope. It's an amazing product and it is sure not to disappoint! product_title: 2 Pack Battery And Charger Kit For Fujifilm FinePix XP70 XP80, XP90, XP120 Waterproof Digital Camera Includes 2 Replacement (1000Mah) Fuji NP-45A, NP-45s Batteries + Ac/Dc Charger + Float Strap + More
review_body:
My order arrived with the same 'battery won't stay in its darn charger' issue others have experienced. Reading reviews I discovered the email/phone of their customer service rep Joseph and gave him a call. Joey was extremely responsive and immediately arranged to ship me a new charger. He expressed concerns as to the mystery of why so many others using that same charger had no issues whatsoever, yet a few of us clearly do. I was curious myself and went back to have another 'much closer' look. Here is what I found:

The Vivitar charger has 3 connection points that one would expect to match up with the same 3 points on the bottom of the battery. They don't, and won't work that way. The good news is that it doesn't matter. Ignore those 3 connection points and just flip the battery over (like backwards) and then lever/push your battery down against the 3 metal poles in the charger itself. As we lever firmly against those poles they will sink down a bit, thus allowing us fully to snap/seat oour battery snugly into the charger, where it will properly hold.

If that still doesn't work for you?

Examine your charger's three post area very carefully in good light. Look for any leftover bits of plastic that may be obstructing your pathway to success. A practically invisible little hunk of (whatever it was) was found on mine near one post. It easily popped off with a fingernail, thus allowing all the posts to fully sink down, and the battery to pop right into place. Just like it should.

The second charger Butterfly shipped me also arrived right on time. I now have two. Hey Joey, if you want that second one back (still unopened/original packaging) feel free to pick it up.

These days, these sorts of little techno-gotchas are a given. The trick is to deal with sellers who will stand behind their stuff. Butterfly did. Thank you again Joseph. The way you handled my complaint did your company proud.

product_title: Lowepro Event Messenger Camera Shoulder Bag
review_body:
The Lowepro Event 150 is marketed as a mild weather bag for a small DSLR or mirrorless kit. Here’s my musings on this wee photo messenger.

EXTERIOR: Inconspicuous and unassuming on the street, the Event looks like a nondescript nylon fabric messenger. Fit and finish are excellent. It’s also surprisingly light: 1 lb 5 oz on my postal scale, a pound lighter than my similarly sized 2013 Timbuk2 XS Snoop. Bottom, sides and top boast closed cell foam padding. The rear slip pocket runs the length of the bag but is only deep enough for tickets or a thin manual. Side pockets are stretchy and fit smokes, flash or a small water bottle. A large zippered pocket under the flap has room for a charger, batteries or a point ’n shoot. The tiny grab handle is an afterthought but is positioned so gear won’t spill out if you forget to secure the lid.

The main flap can be secured via velcro and/or a single clip. I found the flap easy to open and could draw my camera quickly. For increased stealth, the velcro may be silenced by folding over itself.

Although boxy for a messenger, that boxiness gives it enough stability to sit upright on a flat surface. Nevertheless, it’s sufficiently flexible to hug the contour of my back and not bounce while walking. Finally, the nondetachable strap is 2-inches wide and includes a lightly padded 3-inch wide shoulder pad. The strap is comfortable and molds to my chest and shoulders when worn sling style, making a loaded bag seem lighter than it is.

INTERIOR: There are ample pockets for knickknacks and the main compartment may be configured as one, two or three compartments of varying sizes. The brushed cloth interior is soft and grabs the velcro dividers like glue. My EOS 6D with mounted 24-105 4L IS USM, 200 2.8L USM and Speedlite 430EX II fit comfortably (see uploaded image). My EF 70-200 4L IS USM also fit (stowed but not mounted on camera). The two main dividers have hinged flaps for the grip to rest on when the camera is stowed lens down. Dividers are secured by velcro and can be easily repositioned. Three small dividers are included to subdivide the larger compartments, i.e., allow stacking of smaller lenses in a single stall. I rarely carry an iPad—too heavy—but my iPad 2 fits snuggly in the padded slot behind the camera compartment.

WATERPROOFING: The nylon exterior is water resistance and handled dashes in Honolulu rain without a leak. The guard flaps on the sides of the lid prevent water from flowing into the main compartment. However, it lacks a main compartment zipper and rain cover, so the Event is more of a fair weather bag and not a good choice for trekking in rain forests or downpours.

FINAL BLURB: The Event’s appearance will not win fashion kudos but it doesn’t draw attention on the street. It's easy to access, comfortable for hours, narrow enough to squeeze through buses and trains and the price is right. Great small bag for urban photo trekkers.wn. product_title: Tokina 11-16mm f/2.8 AT-X116 Pro DX II Digital Zoom Lens (for Canon EOS Cameras)
review_body:
This version is the updated II type which is optically the same as the I model a newer micro motor is present (it's a little faster) and I don't find it very noise though it isn't silent either. This gives an equivalent full frame. field of view of 18-26mm on a 1.6x crop body (ie Canon)

Build is something Tokina have a good reputation for at that's mirrored here metal casing with chunky rubber grips on the zoom and focus ring, metal mount as expected and a smooth zoom/focus action. This lens uses a "one touch" focus pull the ring back for manual focus or push it forward for normal AF; I find it works quite well though it might take some getting used to.

The main appeal of this lens is two fold firstly it's unusual to have an F2.8 lens for such a wider angle, this would be quite useless though if the lens were optically poor at such an aperture. Good news is that even at F2.8 from 11-16mm the images are very usable with excellent sharpness in "most" of the image area, there is some drop off of sharpness in the extreme corners and edges but not horribly so (not mushed out just softer) stopping down to around F4 improves things with F5.6 really stepping it up. In short for "printable" results (even at fairly large sizes) F2.8 is usable and you shouldn't hesitate to do so in dimmer conditions. For normal daylight stop down as usual though there is little to gain going below F8

Supplied petal hood fits on securely and is well made it can be reversed though this will block much of the focus ring area. This is a lens which does benefit from using it as there are a couple of weaker areas with the lens. Distortion is well controlled a simple mild curve which is easy to correct.

There are a few drawbacks firstly flare can be visible with the sun or bright light sources (lens produces decent sun starts at smaller apertures) other than using the hood or a hand to block stray light there isn't a lot you can do about it. I don't find it a big issue for most shooting conditions it has improved a bit since the Mk I version (new coatings) Second weakness is CA this can be visible at all apertures though more so at the faster ones it doesn't entirely clear up stopping down, this has a distinct "purple" line which tends to show up around higher contrast edges (not always but it's there in with strong highlights) This is relatively easy to remove in post processing even using the auto correction in PS/LR. Min focus isn't anything to rave about (1:11.6) less of an issue as it's for a crop body you can get to about a foot from a subject in the real world still close enough to provide some wild dramatic shots.

A few uses for this lens bar obvious landscape work (it's quite a hard lens to use for this type of shot as foreground is very important) Interior shots are ideal for this lens the faster aperture means you can if required use the lens hand held (tripod is better but you can work it at F2.8) you can get a lot of room into photos with the lens. Wedding another possibility with the faster lens speed available light shooting is realistic. An UWA lens is something of a specialty but also can be quite rewarding it can give a dramatic view that normal lenses can't and it's certainly one that deserves a place in the bag here you get lens speed and sharpness trading a shorter zoom range (it's only 5mm but it's a big difference between the two but at 16mm you are still wide). review_body: [[VIDEOID:418e387c574738bb21a4b0dda5c5180a]]READ: The video messed up during converting for the review. I re-uploaded a new 9 second video that is the correct video. If you're only seeing the 1:00 minute video, this is not the quality of the video. I apologize for this.    The Wespire Action Sports camera is a great quality camera for the price. The camera comes in a box and each piece is packed in it's own plastic bag. I don't need all the accessories at this time but I'm glad that they are on stand-by for when/if I do need them. The instructions are very clear to help you set up your camera. I would recommend turning off the beeping noise and making sure the screen saver goes on, it extends the battery life.. which is about an hour long. I would recommend having a portable charger on stand by, of purchasing an extra battery (I'm not sure if it's available, but I will be looking into this).    Camera operation is simple, and I love that I can press the button even with the water proof case. The LCD screen is great and you can select from different camera modes; video, photo, burst photo and time lapse.    The built in WiFi feature is awesome. If you download the iSmart DV app on your smart phone, you can record and take pictures from your phone. Setting up the WiFi to your phone isn't complicated, you just press the down button and it automatically begins to search for your phone. This is a great feature that I cannot wait to try when I'm riding on the back of my boyfriends motorcycle. I haven't done this yet because th weather has been awful since receiving the camera, but I will post a video from the ride as soon as it happens (hopefully within a couple days).    I purchased a 32GB micro SD card that's made for action sports cameras. It does NOT come with a card so you have to provide your own if you want to use your new camera. The video quality is great so far (again, I will update once I'm able to provide an \\"action shot\\" on a motorcycle).    UPDATE 8/30/2015:I have uploaded a video from a motorcycle ride. I mounted the camera using the attachments on my helmet. During the ride, it was very simple to turn the camera on/off and to connect to WiFi (just be pressing one button) as needed so I can switch from camera to video mode as I wanted to by using the app on my phone (keep in mind, I was the passenger so I do not recommend doing this if you're riding/driving- be safe!). The only thing I didn't like is that I couldn't stream my music because my phone was trying to connect to the cameras software.. so next time, I'll have to download some music to my device if I want to listen to headphones.    The other thing I wanted to point out is that the helmet mounts are straight. I know they make some rounded ones that work better for helmets. product_title: JVC GZ-HD500 80 GB High Definition HDD Camcorder
review_body:
The video quality this camcorder shoots is not truly 1080p.

See the CNET review at http://www.cnet.com/products/jvc-everio-gz-hm300/2/ for further details.

The files do get saved as 1920x1080 pixels, and they are played back as such, but the video itself is not *recorded* in this many pixels. At it's best, it is around half that many. The camcorder then "interpolates up" to 1080p from a recording which is not actually 1080p in its raw state.

It is deceptive that JVC claims the unit has "Full HD 1920x1080 Recording" when it really doesn't.

Also, do not purchase this unit thinking that you will get good image stabilization, because you do not. The camera uses electronic (not optical) image stabilization and the videos are still shaky even with it enabled. If it had optical (instead of electronic) stabilization, the videos might be less shaky when holding the camera in your hand.

product_title: Panasonic Full HD Wi-Fi Enabled 90X Stable Zoom Camcorder with 3-Inch LCD
review_body: Nice camera but with some problems.  Like most cameras these days it doesn't have a viewfinder - only a color LCD display.  This means you need reading glasses to use it properly if you're over 45.  It has an automatic lens cover which is very delicate and flimsy.  After just a few hours of use, one of the two "eyelids" sticks and blocks the lens and I have to manually flick it out of the way.  You can see this in the LCD display but sometimes you don't notice it and get a recording that is partially covered by the lens cap which can't be operated manually.  I may have accidentally put the camera in something that impacted the lens cover or it's just a flawed design.  This camera will fit in your pocket.  You do need to separately purchase an SD flash memory card which can be confusing.  The cards come as straight SD, SDHC, and SDXC.  HC = High Capacity and simply means it is 32 GB.  XC = Extreme capacity and simply means 64 GB.  They also have a speed rating but it's not clear that high speed is required.  Anyway buy a high speed 64 GB card which can be purchased for about $25.  The instructions don't say how much recording you can get at each capacity but the 64 GB card I bought says on the card that it is good for 14 hours of recording which is a lot.  You evidently cannot simply plug the camera into your computer and download videos - according to other reviews you must use the included software which works pretty well.  The only beef I have with the software is that each time you record, it generates a different file rather than continuous video.  Which means there is a break/blank in your video each time you hit the record button.  Also the software is confusing and instead of making it easy to record your videos in sequence on a DVD you can inadvertently order the videos by their digital size which puts everything out of order and wastes a good DVD.  Also there is a blank pause between recordings which is very annoying.  The old tape machines had no such problems - the video was continuous and could not be viewed out of order and there was no blank between recordings.  As with most electronics these days this is a very complicated device and there is no single button to push to make the camera a simple point and shoot.  You have to choose a format as well as "bundled" video options, and also don't forget to activate the optical stabilization which is done separately and a bit confusing!  So it's easy to select the wrong recording format, etc.  It also has a feature to keep the video horizontal which is very useful but confusing to set up and use.  The camera is supposed to turn on and off when you open and close the LCD side panel.  But often this does not turn the camera off and you end up with a video of your shoes and the gum on the pavement.  You need to check the little red light on the back of the camera to make sure it's not still recording when you shut the LCD.  You need a modern TV to view the video directly from the camera since it only has an HDMI output for TV hookups although there are adapters for this I believe.  Most hotels these days have TVs with HDMI so you can view the day's video in your hotel room.  It is a great little camera and I would buy one again.  I find viewers don't like a lot of zooming so I recommend zooming and then hitting the record button rather than the other way around.

product_title: Lowepro Event Messenger Camera Shoulder Bag
review_body:
The Lowepro Event 150 is a mild weather bag designed to fit a medium sized DSLR. Here's my musings on this petite photo messenger.

EXTERIOR: Inconspicuous and unassuming on the street, the Event looks like a nondescript nylon fabric messenger. Yes, the Lowepro logo is embroidered in red, but I nixed it with a few dabs of black leather dye.

Fit and finish are excellent. It's also surprisingly light: 1 lb 5 oz on my postal scale, a pound lighter than my similarly sized 2013 Timbuk2 XS Snoop. Bottom, sides and top boast are protected with closed cell foam padding. The rear slip pocket runs the length of the bag but is so tight it's only good for tickets or a manual. Side pockets are stretchy and big enough for smokes, flash or a small water bottle. A large zippered pocket under the flap has room for a charger, batteries and even a point 'n shoot. The tiny grab handle is an afterthought but is positioned so gear won't spill out if you forget to secure the lid.

The main flap can be secured via velcro and/or a single clip. I found the flap easy to open and could draw my camera quickly. For increased stealth, the velcro may be silenced by folding over itself.

Although boxy for a messenger, that boxiness gives it enough stability to sit upright on a flat surface. Nevertheless, it's sufficiently flexible to hug the contour of my back and not bounce while walking. Finally, the nondetachable strap is 2-inches wide and includes a lightly padded 3-inch wide shoulder pad. The strap is comfortable and molds to my chest and shoulders when worn sling style, making a loaded bag seem lighter than it is.

INTERIOR: There are ample pockets for knickknacks and the main compartment may be configured as one, two or three compartments of varying sizes. The brushed cloth interior is soft and grabs the velcro dividers like glue. My EOS 6D with mounted 24-105 4L IS USM, 200 2.8L USM and Speedlite 430EX II fit comfortably (see uploaded image). My EF 70-200 4L IS USM also fit (stowed but not mounted on camera). The two main dividers have hinged flaps for the grip to rest on when the camera is stowed lens down. Dividers are secured by velcro and can be easily repositioned. Three small dividers are included to subdivide the larger compartments, i.e., allow stacking of smaller lenses in a single stall. I rarely carry an iPad--too heavy--but my iPad 2 fits snuggly in the padded slot behind the camera compartment.

WATERPROOFING: The nylon exterior is water resistance and handled dashes in Honolulu rain without a leak. The guard flaps on the sides of the lid prevent water from flowing into the main compartment. However, it lacks a main compartment zipper and rain cover, so the Event is more of a fair weather bag and not a good choice for trekking in rain forests or downpours.

FINAL BLURB: The Event's appearance will not win fashion kudos but it doesn't draw attention on the street. It's easy to access, comfortable for hours, narrow enough to squeeze through buses and trains and the price is right. Great small bag for urban photo trekkers.wed but not mounted on camera). product_title: Panasonic HC-X1000 4K-60p/50p Camcorder with High-Powered 20x Optical Zoom and Professional Functions (Black)
review_body:
First of all, I have been using Panasonic video cameras in some professional capacity for over 15 years. I absolutely LOVE them.
This is the first offering from Panasonic I have been truly disappointed in. There are two aspects I look for in any camera which are most important: image quality and versatility. This camera has a small image sensor and while the image quality isn't poor, it's nothing to write home about (what's the use of popping for 4k @ 60fps if the image is already limited at the image sensor, huh?) Doesn't make any sense. I guess it all depends on what your standards are and what you are accustomed to. For those who don't know better or have a reference of comparison, it probably doesn't make a difference: you are bound to be thrilled by the image this camera creates. For the rest of us...all I can say is the output from a GH5 at HALF the price at only 4K 30p blows it away with a very noticeable difference.

As far as versatility...I found I was really spoiled by the semi-pro features of my old HCM-150. WTH, NO waveform monitor on this camera? The histogram is a JOKE and there are bare minimum control options for fine tuning the image output. It really feels like they tore apart a cheapie 4K consumer palm-cam and inserted the components into a bigger body housing. Boo, HISS Panasonic. You're BETTER than that! Look, videographers! 4K @ 60 fps...shiney, pretty! YAWN!

The build feels solid enough altho there was a constant nagging feeling in my gut because I KNOW it is high-impact resistant PLASTIC. Once again, my older HCM's spoiled me at about the same price point...approx $3000 for a solid MAGNESIUM body made in JAPAN is now the same price for an EXTRUDED PLASTIC housing made in China? E tu, Panasonic...say it isn't so?

After two weeks I returned this camera for a full refund. I'll wait for the new AG DVX200 which is due out any week now. If you love Panasonic and are serious about the quality of your video, perhaps you should consider doing the same.aps you should consider doing the same.

Uniden really needs to improve/upgrade the app. I have not yet tried Skype to access the video but will since the smart phone app is basically useless.

product_title: Saramonic SmartRig Audio Adapter for Smartphones (Black)
review_body:
I use the SmartRig to connect an XLR microphone to my iPad while livestreaming via the Periscope app. While the iPad has a pretty good open air mic, I sometimes broadcast from pop culture conventions where the ambient noise is too overwhelming. The SmartRig allows me to use a directional mic to decrease that audio clutter.

I first used the SmartRig at San Diego Comic-Con, where I was doing live interviews from a vendor booth. That booth was right next to a busy stage area with big crowds and loud speakers, but I was able to hold conversations on the livestream and be heard perfectly. I was also able to walk around the event with the iPad held aloft well above my head (using the tripod like a monopod) and still provide commentary, because of the external mic. Very handy usage, and not one I'd considered before the event.

The only drawbacks I've found were: 1) the SmartRig is a little clunky hanging from your device on a tripod or while walking around (but that may not affect most users); and 2) the mic output runs a bit hot. Even adjusting volume and testing through the headphone jack, my audio tended to peak and pop. Wasn't a huge issue, I think with some more experimenting I can smooth that out.

All-in-all, I've been very happy with the SmartRig. It's performed well in the field and at home. It's plastic and won't take a beating, but with a little care I think it will hold up.

product_title: Guardzilla  All-In-One Video Security System
review_body:
I have installed my fair share of similar cameras/systems. Dropcam, and the others worked with no problems. They all had similar if not identical procedures: Turn on device, download app, connect to the devices wifi, then the device and your router talk...and viola, its connected and you are good to go.
Not with Guardzilla. Not only has thing failed to connect, half of the times it wouldnt even list my network to connect to. My neighbors were there, but mine weren't. Of course I get out of the app, and my iPhone promptly connects to my network.

It really seems like a hit or miss with this device. I know what I'm doing on my end is right.

I'm wondering if it has something to do with dual-band routers as this device will only see my 2.4ghz band...could be. Either way, it is useless to me.

EDIT: 8/31/15

I really don't like things getting the best of me, so I tackled it again and was finally able to get it to connect...albeit slowly. I have to say, in the end, the video quality is subpar...even on the highest setting. The motion detection system is spotty...even after changing settings. The pet setting doesn't work for me. The images it catches when armed wouldn't let you finger a criminal in a court room if needed. Not to mention the god-awful clicking noise this thing makes when you trip the motion sensor.

For $50 more, do yourself a favor and get a DropCam.

product_title: TELESIN 6" Dome Port for the Gopro Hero3/3+ and Hero4 Underwater Photography--- New Design Accessories Available for the Gopro
review_body:
Considering the alternative at $300 and up, this product is a STEAL!! I first tried it out in the ocean, and it worked perfect. No leaks. Definitely fun to use. There is no vignetting at all. Also pretty rad that it comes with a floating handle and a thumb screw. Also comes with a microfiber cloth, and the box has formed soft foam. That's what I use to store the dome. So SAVE THE BOX unless you have other plans.

Things you should know: Keep in mind there isn't a button to change modes and actually turn the GoPro power ON, like the higher end models. It's hidden by the backside of the dome, so you have to set it up and turn it on BEFORE you put it in the housing.
If you're going for the 50/50 effect (half water half air), you'll want to use this in a body of water that is very calm, like a small lake or pool. This won't have the same effect at all if you're using it in water that is really choppy like the ocean.
If you plan on using it underwater, the water should be VERY clear. You just won't be happy with the footage with you can't see more than 5-10 feet in front of you.
Downsides: The fact you can't change modes without taking it out of the housing is a bummer, but not the end of the world. The actual housing is pretty cheap. Definitely a cheap chinese knockoff. So far so good though.

product_title: DJI Ronin-M 3-Axis Gimbal Stabilizer
review_body:
This is a powerful, lightweight, very well-designed little gimbal. Reading some of the other reviews on here, it seems likely that they didn't balance the camera properly and are relying too heavily on the gimbal motors to compensate. I used a few YouTube videos to help me balance it for the first time, and it took me about 20 minutes. Once I added an HDMI cable running up to a monitor on the handlebars, the balance was thrown off slightly so I spent another two minutes adjusting the balance until the camera sat still without dropping/falling/turning when left still.

The app for iOS is awesome and shows the motor strength of each of the three axes. If any of the motors are operating above 10 (out of 100), you need to re-balance on that axis. I pretty quickly got the motors in the 1-3 range when sitting still, which is awesome. The balancing adjustment knobs are very easy and accurate to adjust, and a huge step up from so many other similar stabilizers on the market.

On my second day of shooting, I found that when panning the camera would sometimes just dive 90 degrees to the left and apparently flip into briefcase mode. I pulled open the app and discovered that the pan axis had gotten bumped when transporting the rig, and the pan axis motor was running around 45-50 (rather than a max of 10). My guess is that the motor was becoming overwhelmed at times (pushing up to 100), and then auto-quit once the load became too heavy, so that was causing it to turn sideways at times. I re-balanced and the rig worked perfectly.

I also love the D-Tap (also known as P-Tap) ports that are all over this thing. I use a D-Tap cable to power my cameras while they're on the Ronin-M, and since that battery can basically go all day, it's perfect. I could plug in my 7" HDMI monitor to D-Tap as well, but I have batteries for that which work just fine.

Overall, the ergonomics and design of this thing are wonderful. Just make sure that it fits your camera, because the cage is just a hair too narrow for the Blackmagic Cinema and Production cameras (though some say it works fine with a RED Epic or Dragon).ur camera, because the cage is just a hair too narrow for the Blackmagic Cinema and Production cameras (though some say it works fine with a RED Epic or Dragon).

My initial review of this was two stars, based on the fact that this only works using Windows ActiveX, something not available to Mac users, and something not all PC users will be comfortable using from a security perspective. If you just try to use the local web interface, everything is in Chinese, with no option to switch to English. However, I've uncovered a much worse issue than any of this which causes me to drop this down to one star, and recommend that NOBODY purchase this. I decided to turn on the outbound firewall on my router to see if anything on my network was dialing out, and discovered that this device has been communicating with at least one external server on its own. In other words, without me doing anything (and, in fact, without me even setting up the device) this camera has been sending information out (I can't tell what) on the internet. There is no good reason to do this, and some pretty nefarious reasons why they might do it.

Given recent headlines on Chinese state-sponsored hacking, I don't think I will ever put another device on my network sold by a Chinese company. (I know that's going to be hard, and the components for a lot of things are made in China, but I think there's less risk of a Chinese supplier trying anything shady with components bound for another company's product.) For all I know, a portion of Chinese consumer electronics companies are fronts for Chinese hackers, trying to get people to put cyber implants on their home networks. To be clear, I am not suggesting this company's device is doing anything malicious, but there is absolutely no reason a device should be talking to anything on the internet without your permission, and without you initiating the connection.

product_title: Belkin F5Z0559 Netcam HD+ & Wemo Insight Switch Bundle
review_body:
Because of their prevalence in retail and my positive experience with Belkin electronic products in the past, I opted for 5 Belkin HD netcams and a handful of Belkin Insight plugs in a home surveillance and automation project. I wish I could go back in time and choose a different platform. There are several reasons:
1) Belkin cameras operate on a different, proprietary software, incompatible with any surveillance apps outside of the poorly designed Belkin apps. This means no way to integrate with other surveillance and security products I use and no way to observe multiple feeds at once and no way to record and store videos on my own hard drive. Most importantly no way to connect cameras to my home automation smart hub which is the center of my home electronics universe and no way to use cams as motion or sound sensors to initiate other smart actions in my home, even though they are motion and sound activated.

Another major problem with the closed system approach to Belkin is that after a measly trial period, no motion activated videos or security incidents can be recorded without paying $10 per month per camera, which in my case is $50. What are the odds of me randomly logging into my cameras at the exact moment of a security incident? What's worse, the mobile notifications that accompany motion-activated events is tied to this same subscription model, making them effectively worthless for security without a subscription.

The HD image is clear, IF and ONLY IF my home wifi is running at really high speeds with minimal interference, and my mobile device for viewing the feed is on a solid high speed wifi network or very near a Verizon LTE-capable tower. Night vision works fairly well even in very low light.

Wish the microphones were more sensitive, although the speakers are more than capable for 2-way audio.

product_title: Sto-Fen Omni-Bounce OM-EW Flash Diffuser (for Canon Speedlite 430EX, 430EX II, 430EX III)
review_body:
I am only a hobbyist photographer and not a "pro" by any means. As a matter of fact, my "Canon 6D" camera is far smarter than I can ever hope to be. (At least I'm not crazy, my mother had me tested). As much as I really like my "Canon 430 EXII" flash, I wanted to soften the light in my indoor "people" pictures a bit more than just bouncing the flash would do. That is why I got this diffuser and I'm glad I did.

There are several of these "after market" diffusers offered for the "Canon 430 EXII" flash. Many are cheaper and some are far more expensive and all seem to have some reviews indicating problems with the "fit" to the flash. I chose this one by "Stofen" because it was both "middle of the road" in price and seemed to have the best chance of satisfaction for "fit" to the "Canon 430 EXII" flash according to my reading of a lot of reviews.

Well I can safely say I am very pleased with this "Stofen" diffuser that I received. Now, I obviously cannot speak for ALL "Stofen" diffusers but the one I received works very well for me. It does fit my "Canon 430 EXII" flash very well. The diffuser is of course plastic but is just flexible enough to fit my flash without falling off and does not cause any scratching or damage to my flash head during install or removal. I primarily use my "430 EXII" flash only in "TTL" mode and this diffuser works well for me. It does soften the light a bit more and does decrease shadows and harsh lighting I may sometimes get even with "bounce" flash. Now again, I am NOT a "pro". I can take just as many lousy pictures as I can good ones when I get lucky. For my old eyes and the fun I have taking pictures, this diffuser works very well for me.

Now as I mentioned, I am NOT a "pro" so I cannot whip out a bunch of charts and graphs or rattle off a bunch of "f stop" numbers or quantify any "luminosity" values. All I can say is I am very pleased with this diffuser. It fits my "Canon 430 EXII" very well and softens the light on my indoor flash pictures just as I wanted it to do.

I would recommend this diffuser.quantify any "luminosity" values. All I can say is I am very pleased with this diffuser. It fits my "Canon 430 EXII" very well and softens the light on my indoor flash pictures just as I wanted it to do. I would recommend this diffuser.

I ended up having to unplug the connections a couple days later and they where very difficult to unplug, not possible with just my hands, I had to use tools.

This time I put a small amount of plumbers silicone grease on the probes of the male plugs and they connected right together with the normal amount of effort of an MC4 connector, easily plugged together and unplugged using just your hands.

Do yourself a big favor and put a little silicone grease on the male plugs before mating these adapters. Other then that no other issues, I'm not even knocking a star off for the tight fit and lack of lubrication as it's easily remedied.

product_title: Feisol Classic CT-3371 Rapid 3-Section Tripod, Large - Supports 55 lbs
review_body: I'd been using a medium-sized carbon-fiber tripod (the Giottos MT-8361), and overall I was satisfied with it. It was rated for more than the weight of my usual gear, and the tripod was able to adjust the middle column to just about any position (great for macro shots). It was fine for the 100-300 f/4, but it wasn't quite up to the 300 f/2.8. I needed a bigger tripod. The gold standard of tripods are Gitzo's - and there's a reason they're the gold standard - they cost their weight in gold! I was looking at spending north of $900 for the kind of tripod I wanted. As I was collecting all my change to make a purchase, I kept noticing ads and reviews for Feisol tripods. They're fairly new on the scene, tripod-wise, but have been making CF legs for other tripod manufacturers for some time. Because their tripods are so new, it was difficult to find many reviews, but the ones I did find were universally enthusiastic about their tripods. And the best part? Feisol prices are half of what Gitzo charges. I found a model that fit my needs (the CT-3371) and pulled the trigger. The tripod was shipped from the US distributor and arrived in only a few days. My initial impression? WOW. This thing is a monster. The legs are three to four times the size of my previous CF tripod, and when full extended, the thing is almost taller than I am. And it's stable - my gear doesn't budge. I could get another one and hang a hammock between them. I shoot with other photographers with big Gitzo tripods who were initially very skeptical of using any tripod other than a Gitzo, but all have been impressed with the build quality and finish of the Feisol. This may be the last tripod I ever buy, and will handle any camera/lens combo I put on this monster. If you need a monster tripod capable of handing a big load, check out Feisol - you won't be disappointed.

product_title: Ambient Weather BC-1900 Intelligent 9V Battery Charger, Analyzer and Diagnostic Center for NiCad and NiMh Batteries

I've purchased two weather stations from Ambient Weather and stand behind them 100%.  What I like the most about the BC-1900 was that it could charge NiCd, NiMH, or Li-ion battery types.  I currently use NiMH, but I would like to check out the Li-ion batteries in the near future.  I love how this is a smart charger and has several functions (modes).  It can Charge, Discharge, Refresh, and Test.  You can hook up to 4 batteries at a time and each one can be in its own mode and display setting.  While the batteries are connected, the display can show the charge/discharge voltage, current, elapsed time, or accumulated capacity.  I’ve had no problems with this charger and I had to use it several times already to recharge all my batteries.  As with all battery chargers make sure you never charge unattended.  This one doesn’t have battery temperature protection due to the size.  So far this has been a wise investment and I’ve been very happy with the quality.

product_title: Samsung SDS-P5122 16 Channel All-in-one DVR Security System
review_body:
This system is working very well for us, monitoring a 2nd home. However, initially, while testing it locally, the DVR started making grinding noises. It was fixed under warranty, no questions asked, and an extra camera and cable was provided as well. Setup, for access over the Internet, was not as easy as it could be either initially or in the 2nd home. I had to spend time on the phone with a tech to get it running initially, but the tech was helpful and polite. For the 2nd home, we had to break down and get a static IP address there. Since then it has worked very well. The software is not the easiest to set up or run and the directions are confusing. Happily there has been an upgrade to the S/W you access via Internet Explorer so I can now do everything but restart the machine if the standby battery runs down in a blackout. Daytime color imaging is very good, and the nighttime IR is adequate. I am planning to upgrade one camera to be able to have a better night-time view of the road. Wiring the 2nd home was a problem but that is not due to unit. I was asked "Why not use wireless cameras?" and the answer is I would have the SAME wiring problem getting power to the cams. As I was having an alarm system installed, too, the alarm company agreed to install the DVR system for me and they did a fine job.

Pros: Nice images, clean-look cameras, great, responsive support and repairs, software that so far is reliable, can access recorded images remotely, can control and modify settings remotely. Solid system.

product_title: [Fuji Instax Mini 90 Case] -- CAIUL Comprehensive Protection Camera Case Bag For Fujifilm Instax Mini 90 Neo Classic Instant Film Camera With Soft PU Leather Material
review_body:
The case fits my Fuji Instax Mini 90 camera like a glove. The people who are leaving poor ratings for this case because they purchased it for another camera are frankly idiots. It clearly states in the description and the TITLE ITSELF that it is for the Fuji Instax Mini 90. It's like buying a game for an XBox and then getting upset when it doesn't work with my Playstation.

The faux leather material that the case is made from is good enough where an untrained eye would have difficulty determining whether it's real leather or not. The material is very pliable yet stiff enough to retain its shape around the camera. I do like the brown contrasting with the black color of my camera. On the strap itself, it almost appears that it's made from a stiffer material - meaning that after a week the strap is still retaining the creases from being folded up in the packaging. It would have been nicer if they just rolled it up instead of folding it.

There were some complaints about the magnetic bits that hold the front flap to the case to cover the lens. I don't seem to have a problem with the flap freeing itself in normal use. The magnets appear to be strong enough to keep the flap in place, but weak enough to allow you to free the flap with a single hand.

For future iterations, I would love to see a sleeve or a pocket to carry accessories like an additional film cartridge, or enough space to slip in a stack of photos along with an ID, credit card, and some cash.

product_title: Fujifilm XF 27mm F2.8 Compact Prime Lens
review_body:
Wonderful lens; small and sharp. I moved to the Fuji X system from an M-mount camera, where lenses are small and well-made. My first X mount lens, the [[ASIN:B00EZ8BEXK Fujinon XF 23mm F1.4 R]] sold me on the system, with beautiful image quality. However, that lens is huge, almost DSLR-size. I wanted something small and light to carry around from day-to-day and while traveling, and the 27mm lens is just perfect!

I love the images and the f/2.8 is not limiting at all in most situations. The field of view, with about a 41mm (35mm equivalent) is well pared with the 14mm lens (21mm equivalent), and might be the only two lenses that I really need.

Yes, the silver version of this lens looks great on the silver and black bodies, as well as the all-black Fuji cameras. I have a black X-E2, and my silver version of this lens adds a bit of elegance.

I don't find the lack of an aperture ring limiting, in fact, for this lens I am happy without it. I travel a bit leading groups overseas, so I am often handing my camera to strangers and tour leaders to get a group photo of us all. With this lens I don't have to worry about someone changing the aperture by accident, thinking it is the zoom ring. You can set a function button to easily switch between auto and manual aperture control.

Just buy this!
